## 6ew. The rows whose roll was taken for the whole cell

6es recorded this as a successor: *"A self-control row's other clauses
are unsaid."* `reported` gave `UNREAD` only to a row outside `known()`
that printed no self-control roll. A row that did print one said
nothing, on the reading that the roll is the row.

### The census

A throwaway test (deleted after it ran) walked every catalogue row with
`selfControl` through `reported`. **30 rows** carry the field, all in
`disadvantages.json`. Two are in `known()` (Loner and Workaholic, by
their social clauses) and say what they leave out. **The other 28 said
nothing**, beside cells such as Reckless's *"-1 to any roll where
caution would be smarter"*, Reluctant Killer's *"-4 to hit recognizable
people with deadly force (-2 if face hidden); cannot Aim"*,
Absent-Mindedness's -3 and Nightmares' *"lose 1 FP each morning"*. I
first wrote "29 of 31". The reviewer counted 30 in the JSON, and the
census's own list held 30.

The same census answered 6ev's attack-roll successor: with every
catalogue row held, `TraitEffects.modifiers` returns nothing for all 19
COMBAT SKILLS keys. Every combat skill is DX-controlled and no
`SKILL_BONUSES` or `CATEGORY_BONUSES` row names one. So the Attack
dialog's missing trait term costs nothing today. Reluctant Killer is
the first row that would make it matter, and it would come in as a
declared clause, not as an unconditional term.

### What was built

- **`TraitEffects.ROLLED_ONLY`**: *"its price and its self-control roll
  aside, this app applies nothing this row prints, so the rest of its
  text is the table's to apply"*. It is one sentence for all 28, not
  five hand-written reasons, for `UNREAD`'s reason: a reason per row is
  a claim about the app that nothing re-reads (6eq). Curious, which
  prints only its roll, gets it too. Its *"or investigate any mystery"*
  is the table's to apply, so the sentence is true of it.
- **The sentence is decided by `SelfControl.checksFor`**, the code that
  offers the roll (the review's MEDIUM). `checksFor` rolls DISADVANTAGE
  rows only, so a quirk named `Reckless` is offered no roll and gets
  `UNREAD`. A second predicate on `row.selfControl` would have told it
  the roll was applied.

### The sweep found a row that could not find itself

The review asked for a sweep over all 28 instead of a sample of five,
with `checksFor` asserted on each. It went red on one row:
**`Compulsive Behavior (Indulge Evil Desires) SC 6`**. `catalogueName`
strips a trailing integer as a level (`Alertness 1`), so the row's own
name resolved to `... SC`, which matches nothing. The builder sells
this row (`PurchasableTraits.offered()`), and a character who bought it
got no cell on the Traits tab, no self-control roll and no note, and
was still charged for it. It is the only catalogue row whose name ends
in a number. **A row's own name now resolves to itself**, ahead of the
strip, and `every catalogue row name resolves to itself` pins it.

### Review

Codex was out until Oct 9, 02:02 and the free panel's gateway was down
(`[qa] fetch failed`), so one review sub-agent read the diff. The
verdicts were CHANGE, SHIP, CHANGE: the MEDIUM above, the miscount, a
`startsWith` assertion that compared a constant with its own text, and
the sample. All were taken. **The `catalogueName` fix came after the
review and no reviewer has read it.**

**Codex then answered (Oct 9, 11:15)**, on `5fe2b41..127532d` and on
`63e6290..a50baed` in one `codex exec`. **6ev: SHIP** on every question.
Its strongest objection to the DX row is that *"Brawling or DX"* could
mean DX only when untrained. The cell does not settle that, and the
screen states the reading. **6ew: one MEDIUM, taken.** The exact-match line
returned the SHEET's casing, and `reported` checks `known()`
case-sensitively, so `PHOBIA (SPECIFY)` was told that a rule it applies
was unread. The line now returns the row's own spelling. The guard
upper-cases every row name, and its RED listed every row in the
catalogue. Codex SHIPped the `checksFor` predicate and found no
initialisation cycle between the two objects.

### Verification

1866 Kotlin (1306 `core:rules`, 540 `app`, 20 `core:model`), green from

## 6ev. The operand the parry cell had printed all along

6eu named this successor as *"the Defend dialog takes no default"*, and
asked whether a default parries. The first half of that question was the
wrong question. The bare-hand parry is not a default at all.

### What the Defend dialog did

It built unarmed parry rows from the styles a sheet owns: Brawling, Boxing,
Wrestling. A sheet with none got no row and this note, written in 6et:
*"Brawling defaults to DX-2 untrained; this screen offers no parry from a
default, which is a gap and not a ruling."*

Book line 2473 is the Parry (Unarmed) row's FORMULA cell: *"Brawling or DX
÷ 2 + 3"*. `defenses.json` has carried that string since the table was
extracted, and `tools/test_tools.py` pins it. No Kotlin read the second
operand. A grep for the string across `docs/` returned nothing either:
this log discusses the row's Notes cell at length and never its formula.
6ap found that the Notes cell holds three rules and the code did one. The
cell beside it held two operands and the code did one.

### The census, before the review

*"Brawling if held, else DX"* and *"the better of the two"* disagree only
where a held Brawling sits below played DX. A throwaway test walked all 23
premades through every pathway chain: 2024 states, 1124 holding Brawling,
none below DX. It was deleted after it ran, and its number is in
`ParryBlock.bareHandParry`'s KDoc with that provenance.

### The design review

**Codex ran out mid-review.** `codex exec` returned
`ERROR: You've hit your usage limit ... try again at Oct 9th, 2026 2:02 AM`
after one interim note: the table permits a DX parry, does not say *"only
without Brawling"*, and names Brawling for the weapon penalty. The free
panel was down too (`[qa] fetch failed`, the gateway was not running). The
third gate is one review sub-agent, and it answered: ship all three parts,
change one.

- **The gate was mine, not the book's.** I proposed showing the DX row
  only on a sheet with no Brawling. The cell says *"or"*. The row is
  withheld only where a held Brawling already parries at least as well,
  because the two rows then differ in nothing.
- **DX itself, not Brawling's default halved.** Where the book means a
  penalised operand it prints one: *"Skill defaults to Shield/DX or
  Brawling-2"* (2537). So Versatile's +1 has nothing to add to.
- **The −3 against a weapon is a reading, and the screen says so.** The
  Notes cell's subject is *"Brawling"* and no line prints *"unarmed parries
  weapons at -3"*. DX takes it because it stands in Brawling's slot of the
  formula and Boxing is the one exemption named. Without it an untrained
  hand at DX 10 turns a knife at 8 beside a brawler's 5. The reviewer's
  case against: *"absurd"* is no warrant, since Wrestling 12 parries at 7
  beside DX 12's 9.
- **Its HIGH: a DX row drawn beside `parries` misses everything that reads
  the list.** The shot filter, the cumulative penalty, the stepper and the
  boost picker all iterate it. So the row is an entry in it.
- **The Acrobatic Dodge has no training restriction.** Line 2483 says
  *"Roll vs. Acrobatics"*, and line 424 *"You can attempt most skills even
  without training"*.

### What was built

- `UnarmedStyle.BARE_HANDS`, and `ParryBlock.bareHandParry(dx, brawling)`:
  `floorDiv(dx, 2) + 3`, or null where a held Brawling parries as well.
  `versusWeaponPenalty` names every style now, where an `else` had settled
  Wrestling's −3 without saying so.
- **`unarmedParries(skillLevels, dx)`** in the dialog: the held styles,
  then `Parry (DX, bare hands)`. A note under the rows quotes the formula
  cell and states the two readings.
- **`unskilledParriers`**: a carried melee weapon no skill wields is named,
  with the reason. Line 2468 prints *"Weapon Skill ÷ 2 + 3"* and no second
  operand, which is the difference between the two rows and the reason an
  armed default stays out.
- **`acrobaticsFor(skillLevels, untrained)`**: the sheet's Acrobatics, or
  the row `SkillDefaults.offeredTo` already composed. The dialog rebuilds
  no DX-6, so Versatile's +1 arrives inside the level. This is the fourth
  consumer of a default.
- The 6et note is gone. It could not be reached: `parries` is never empty.

### The diff review

The same sub-agent gate, with the eight files named. SHIP on the rows,
with every reachable state enumerated. FIX on the roll.

- **HIGH, taken: the level matched the Skills tab and the roll did not.**
  That tab rolls with `conditionsFor + TraitEffects.modifiers +
  circumstances`. Defend passed `conditionsFor` alone, and Perfect Balance
  is +2 on Acrobatics. Pickpocket has DX 10, Perfect Balance and no
  Acrobatics: target 4 in Defend, 6 on Skills.
- **The gap was not new, and this slice made it reachable.** The trained
  path had skipped the trait term since the control was written. No
  premade could show it: the one sheet with Perfect Balance has no
  Acrobatics, and the control refused a sheet without the skill. Offering
  a control to more sheets is a change to every term its roll was missing.
- **`acrobaticRoll(skill, conditions, traits, dice)`** composes both
  terms. The test was watched failing on the number first: *expected 6 but
  was 4*. The GM's circumstance chips stay on the Skills tab's dialog, and
  the KDoc says so.
- **Eight LOWs on sentences, all taken.** Two of mine said the Shield Bash
  line was *"two lines on"*. It is 64. `TraitEffects` still said *"all
  three"* consumers. The guide promised a note for any unskilled weapon,
  and a firearm gets none.
- **One inferred LOW changed a KDoc of mine.** The reviewer read
  `PotionDigestion` as re-folding a chain from the bought attributes, so
  *"a DX bought later"* would not outrun a grant. I did not verify that.
  The KDoc now names only the shape the census looked for and did not
  find.

## 6eu. The attack a default can make

6et shipped the untrained roll to one consumer and said so: a player could
roll Brawling from the Skills tab and could not throw the punch. This slice
is the second consumer. It also takes back a refusal 6et made an hour
earlier, because the reason for it does not hold on this screen.

### What the Attack dialog did

It listed `skillLevels`, the skills a sheet owns. Picking one arms it:
`Damage.attacksFor` gives the unarmed table, which only Brawling and Boxing
have, and `Weapons.forSkill` gives chapter 8's weapons. So a character
without Brawling had no punch, and one handed a revolver without Guns
(Revolver) had no shot.

### The design review

Codex, through `codex exec`, on a written decomposition and no diff: CHANGE
on all three questions.

- **The list is "the attacks supported here".** I proposed offering the
  untrained skills with a printed attack, and asked whether that criterion
  was the book's or mine. It is this app's boundary. The book prints a
  COMBAT SKILLS banner of nineteen, Fast-Draw and Shield among them, and a
  default line for a Shield Bash (2537), and neither decides which skills
  this dialog can show damage for. Eight can: Brawling, Boxing, Knife,
  Axe/Mace, Broadsword and three Guns.
- **Apply the mastery, to the weapon actually in hand.** 6et named three
  potion lines and applied none, on the reason *"this list does not know
  what is in hand"*. Here one is. Warrior (Twilight Giant 9): *"every
  weapon is treated as known at effective DX (no default penalty) from the
  moment it is picked up"*. Weapon Master (7): the same *"instantly"*, and
  *"a strict upgrade to and replacement of the Warrior's Combat Mastery"*.
  The review's two HIGHs were about WHEN: Brawling arms a truncheon and
  opens on a fist, so *"this skill has a weapon"* would have given a punch
  the weapon's level; and putting a weapon down lowers the level under a
  Deceptive Attack already bought, which throws on Roll.
- **Only the Warrior has a clause left over.** *"Weapons used repeatedly in
  a session are treated as known at default +2"* is said as not applied,
  since nothing here counts uses. The Weapon Master *"requires no
  warm-up"*.
- **A false sentence in the dialog's own KDoc**: *"this book tags no skill
  as a combat skill"*. Line 1668 is the banner. `TraitEffects` cited the
  same premise for a refusal of its own.

### What was built

- `SkillDefaults.attacks(untrained)`: the rows with an unarmed table or a
  weapon row.
- `SkillDefaults.WeaponMastery`, `masteryFor(pathway, sequence)` and
  `mastered(level, weaponInHand, mastery, dx)`. With a weapon in a
  master's hand a level below DX becomes DX. Versatile's +1 does not come
  along: *"treated as known"* is not a roll at a default.
- `SkillDefaults.toolNote`: the Harvest Priest's farming-tool line, which
  stays unapplied because the weapon table marks no row as a tool.
- `Attacks.atLevel(plan, level)`: a fourth plan transition. A Deceptive
  Attack the new level cannot afford is dropped to zero, never trimmed.
- **The dialog** lists the untrained rows after the owned ones, each with
  *"untrained, DX-4"* under it. One `levelWith(weaponInHand)` feeds the
  header, the stepper's ceiling, Boxing's bonus, the modifiers and the
  roll. Both hand changes move the plan through `atLevel`. The weapon line
  prints *"no parry offered without the skill"* where it printed a parry.
- `PLAIN_ROLL`, the Skills list's caveat, now sends a punch to Attack.

### The diff review

Codex again: FIX, two MEDIUMs.

- **Taken: the mastery lifted only an untrained skill.** One point in
  Axe/Mace is DX-1. A Warrior who trained with the axe swung it at DX-1,
  and one who never had swung it at DX. *"Every weapon"* is the book's
  phrase, so the line is a floor at DX for a bought skill too.
- **Declined: a dialog regression test** for the two `atLevel` call sites.
  Composables are device-only in this repo (section 6), and one screen is
  not the reason to add `androidx.compose.ui.test`. The transition is
  unit-tested, and the device pass below drives the weapon-down path with
  two Deceptive steps bought and then rolls. The fist path needs a master
  whose Brawling sits below DX, which a potion's frozen grant can produce
  and no premade does. It runs the same call and was not driven.

### After both reviews: a parry of 9 on one screen and 8 on the other

The final check traced what the diff review's own fix had done. The floor
lifts a bought skill, the weapon line under the header read the lifted
level, and `Weapons.parryFor` priced a parry from it. Defend prices the
same weapon off the sheet's level, through `Weapons.levelFor`. A Warrior
at DX 12 with one point in Axe/Mace would have read `parry 9` in Attack
and `8` in Defend. Before the fix nothing could disagree, because every
lifted row was untrained and printed no parry at all.

- **The weapon line prices its parry from the skill's own level**, and
  says so where a mastery lifted the attack: *"parry 8 (the skill's own,
  not lifted)"*. Whether a weapon *"treated as known at DX"* parries at DX
  is the open question, and it is answered on both screens or neither.
- **My own device pass could not have shown it.** The seeded Librarian's
  DX is 11, and at an odd DX the two parries coincide. The proof needs an
  even one: Beat Cop as a Warrior, DX 12, Axe/Mace bought at 11, a Hand
  Axe carried. Attack prints the line above, and Defend prints `Parry
  (Hand Axe)` `8`.

**A fix for a review finding is new code no review has read.** The parry
line is a composable, so nothing but that device pass covers it.

## 6et. The roll nobody on the sheet could make

6eq named this, and 6er and 6es each carried it forward: book 2540 prints
*"Default: DX-2 if untrained"* for Brawling, and `SkillLadder.defaultFor`,
which the journal called its implementation, has had no production caller
since M0. This slice gives it one. It is wider than the sentence that named
it, because the sentence was one row of a table the app never rolled.

### What the book prints

- **Chapter 2, lines 423-442.** *"You can attempt most skills even without
  training. This is called using the default."* Easy is Attribute -4,
  Average -5, Hard -6, and Very Hard is *"No default — cannot attempt
  untrained"*. The worked example is Lockpicking at IQ 9: *"IQ - 5 = 4"*.
- **Chapter 5 prints three lines of its own.** Brawling, DX/Easy:
  *"Default: DX-2 if untrained"* (2540, and 2630 in the summary). Boxing,
  DX/Average: *"Default DX-5"*, which agrees with the table. Wrestling,
  DX/Average: *"No default"* (2642).
- **Chapter 4, 3559.** *"Divination Arts defaults to Ritualistic Magic-2 and
  vice versa. A character with one skill at 12+ can attempt the other at
  -2."*
- **Appendix A, 9738-9739**, restates the table as one row: *"Attribute -4
  to -6"*.
- **Line 440-441**: no default either for *"any skill the GM rules requires
  specialist knowledge before you can even attempt it"*.

### What the app did

It rolled only what a sheet owned: published, bought or granted by a
potion. Three screens said an untrained roll was *"the GM's call"*, and
`DefenseDialog`'s KDoc gave the reason as the appendix's RANGE and called
the fix *"a policy for 158 skills, not a branch for this one"*. The range
is the table's two ends. The policy is this slice.

### The design review

Codex, through `codex exec`, on a written decomposition and no diff:
CHANGE, SHIP, CHANGE.

- **The table is chapter 2's**, and the appendix summarises it.
- **Divination Arts is a reading, to be said as one.** I proposed reading
  3559 as Brawling's line is read: a skill's own line replaces the table's,
  so SPI-6 is not offered. The review's MEDIUM: the line does not say
  *only*, so that is *"less conclusive than Wrestling's express refusal"*.
  It is the reading `Divination.crossDefaultFor` has made since 6az, and
  the list now says on screen that it makes it.
- **Three potion blocks print "no default penalty" for a weapon**, which
  my formula ignored: Warrior and Weapon Master (Twilight Giant 9 and 7)
  and Harvest Priest (Mother 7). Apply them or name them.
- **One consumer is enough for one slice**, with the objection said out
  loud: a player can roll Brawling and cannot complete the attack.
- **Ten sentences go stale**, listed by file and line. All ten are
  corrected in the same commits.

### What was built

- `SkillDefaults`, a new rules object. `offered(owned, attributeLevel,
  defaultBonus)` returns every printed skill the character does not hold
  and the book gives a default, each with its level and where it came
  from. `offeredTo(character)` asks it of the character as played. A
  character who owns nothing is offered 149 of the 158: less the seven
  Very Hard rows, Wrestling, and Divination Arts.
- **Owned is the same name and specialization at any difficulty.** Five
  potion grants disagree with chapter 3 about a difficulty, and the
  catalogue prints no name and specialization twice, which a test pins.
  An instance of an open row leaves the open row on offer.
- **Divination Arts is asked of `Divination.divinationLevelFor`**, never
  recomputed, so the Skills tab cannot offer what the Divine tile refuses.
- **Versatile's +1 is inside every default.** Its sheet note, *"this app
  offers no other roll at a default"*, is removed: the second false
  sentence that one trait has carried.
- **The three weapon lines are named and not applied**, each in its own
  words. Which skill a weapon uses is a property of the weapon in hand.
- **The screen.** One row at the foot of the Skills tab, *"Roll a skill
  this sheet does not have"*, opens a list with a filter. A pick goes to
  the sheet's own `RollDialog` through `SkillRoll.at`, labelled *"Acrobatics
  (untrained, DX-6)"*, so it takes the trackers, the traits and the GM's
  circumstances as any other skill does.
- **The Defence dialog's two notes** say what is missing rather than whose
  call it is: this screen takes no roll at a default.

### The diff review

Codex again: FIX, one MEDIUM and two LOWs, all taken.

- **MEDIUM: the weapon note flattened three lines into one.** Harvest
  Priest's is *"any farming or gardening tool as a weapon"*, and the note
  said *"with a weapon"*. Each block carries its own scope now, and the
  test quotes the block.
- **LOW: I wrote that a mortal's SPI of 0 "does the gating"**, and it does
  not. `SuccessRoll` gives a 3 or a 4 its critical success at any target,
  so a mortal's Spiritual Perception at -5 succeeds one roll in 54. That
  is this app's standing reading of the book's *"always succeeds"*, and
  the comment says so.
- **LOW: no test rolled a default.** One does: a negative target through
  `SkillRoll.at`, and Perfect Balance lifting an untrained Acrobatics.

### After both reviews: five premades were offered their own skill

The final check asked what I had measured "an owned skill is not offered"
on. One premade, twice. A probe ran every premade as printed, and one of
them through all 88 potion blocks, and listed every offered row sharing a
name with an owned skill: 55 pairs. Fifty-three are two skills by the
book's own shape, an open row beside an instance or a name it prints more
than once. **Two are not.** `academic_researcher`, `antiquarian_dealer`,
`monastery_scholar`, `occult_scholar` and `university_librarian` print
*"Mathematics"* or *"History (Occult)"*, the book prints *"Mathematics
(Applied)"* and a bare, closed *"History"*, and the list offered each its
own skill again at IQ-6.

- **The rule is the catalogue's shape, not the two names.** Where the book
  prints one row of a name, that row is not open, and one of the two
  spellings has no specialization, the owned skill can be nothing else.
  Fast-Draw (Revolver) beside the book's only Fast-Draw (Pistol) stays two
  skills, and so does an instance of an open row.
- **A placeholder grant covers nothing, on purpose.** Warrior's *"Armoury
  (any)"* and Hunter's *"Survival (any terrain)"* leave the open row on
  offer. The player chose one and the app was not told which.
- **A sheet name the book does not print matches nothing.** *"Engineer
  (Steam)"* does not cover Engineering. Recorded, never repaired.
- The probe is a test now, over the same corpus. Four mutations of the new
  check, four caught, `ran=101`.

Neither review could have found it from the diff: the fixture spellings
are not in it. **A reviewer reads what the diff shows; the corpus has to
be asked.** The `feat(rules)` commit's body also overclaims. *"Two screens
cannot give one roll two numbers"* is true of a Divination Arts the
character does not own, and only of that.

### Seen and not touched

## 6es. The complement of `known()`

6er named this first of two successors: Official Beyonder, a 15-point
advantage the builder sells, was in no collection, no test and no slice,
and the instruction was to **ask what else is in the complement of
`TraitEffects.known()`**. This slice lists that complement for the first
time and acts on four things in it.

### The census

The query is every row of `advantages.json` and `disadvantages.json` whose
name is not in `TraitEffects.known()`, run as a throwaway test at `c3011e6`.
**148 of the 198 rows**: 65 advantages and 83 disadvantages. 28 of the 83
print a self-control roll, which `SelfControl` offers from the row itself.
47 of the remaining 120 print a signed number.

Two readings of that list were wrong before they were recorded.

- **"24 of the premades' 50 advantage rows say nothing" is not 24 gaps.**
  Most of them are applied in full and correctly have nothing to report
  (Alertness, Hard to Kill, Outdoorsman). What the number does measure is
  the sheet: those 24 rows were printed nowhere on it.
- **A skill-name pass found ten rows and is too narrow to be a census.** It
  needs a catalogue skill name in the cell, so it cannot see *"rural
  navigation rolls"*, *"Vision rolls"* or *"Perception rolls while
  sleeping"*, and one of its ten was *Acting* inside *"Acting Method"*.

### Four things in the complement

- **Two rows production applies by name.** Night Eyes, which
  `TraitEffects.darknessReduction` applies from the same object, and
  Spiritual Fortitude, which `Corruption.maxFor` has read since M4. Found
  by grepping both source trees for `levelOf(`, `catalogueName(` and a name
  equality, then diffing against `known()`. Both are in it now. Both
  clauses of Night Eyes are applied already (`DarknessCause.DIM_LIGHT`).
  This is the shape of `c0b65f3`, and the fifth and sixth instance of the
  failure `known()`'s own KDoc records.
- **Three cells that name printed skills and no circumstance.** Acute
  Social Awareness (*"+2 to all Body Language and Detect Lies rolls"*),
  Former Military Officer (*"Leadership and Tactics at +1"*) and
  Photographic Instinct (*"Photography rolls at +2"*). All three are
  `SKILL_BONUSES` rows now. Every guard on that map walks the map, so a
  cell no map names was checked by nothing. The clause guard then demanded
  their leftovers, and three are reported: the officer's contacts and
  courtesies, and the photographer's instinct.
- **Official Beyonder, refused whole.** See the design review.
- **Everything else, which said nothing.** See *the sheet*.

### The design review

Codex, through `codex exec`, on a written decomposition and no diff. Three
questions, three verdicts.

- **CHANGE: Official Beyonder is refused, all four skills.** I favoured
  applying each *+N* to a skill the character already owns, on the argument
  that both readings agree there: chapter 3 writes a roll bonus as *"+N to
  X"*, and chapter 6 (5449-5462) reads a bare *+N* as *"Attribute + N"*, or
  *"skill level + N"* for a skill already known. The review's HIGH: 5458
  says that of a potion's entry and requires the same name and difficulty,
  so borrowing it for an advantage cell is a hypothesis. **Agreement
  between two proposed readings does not establish the rule.** The phrase
  *"<Skill> +N"* as a list item occurs nowhere else outside the potion
  tables. Priced as grants on this book's ladder the four skills are
  4 + 16 + 16 + 8 = 44 points against the row's 15, which discriminates
  nothing (6cd). The row is in `UNAPPLIED` with that reason.
- **Both name joins are sound and wait on the reading.** *"Revolver"* is
  `Guns (Revolver)` and *"Hidden Lore (Beyonders)"* is a name with a
  specialization. `SKILL_BONUSES` joins on the name alone, so a later
  slice that applies them must match the specialization too.
- **CHANGE: list every advantage, and say something of the unread ones.**
  A cell that prints a number with no caveat reads as counted. The review
  asked for one reusable line rather than a reason per row.
- **SHIP the three skill bonuses.** *"in formal settings"* qualifies the
  courtesies, not the +1.

### What was built

- `known()` gains `NIGHT_EYES` and `Corruption.FORTITUDE`.
- Three `SKILL_BONUSES` rows, two `PARTLY_APPLIED` entries, one line of
  prose named in the clause guard.
- `UNAPPLIED["Official Beyonder"]`.
- `TraitEffects.UNREAD`, which `reported` returns for a held trait whose
  row is outside `known()` and prints no self-control roll. It fires on
  114 rows: 59 advantages and 55 disadvantages.
- `TraitEffects.held(traits, kind)`: one `HeldTrait` per trait, with the
  book's cell and its notes.
- **The sheet.** The Traits tab printed `reported(traits)` and then every
  drawback. An advantage with nothing to report was nowhere on the sheet,
  and its cell was on no screen: the gallery card and the builder show a
  name. That is 6am's finding one list over. It prints one row per
  held advantage now (*"name — N pts"*, the cell), then the drawbacks as
  before, and each row carries its own notes under it. A note on the
  whole cell prints the caveat alone. A note on one clause quotes the
  clause first.

### The diff review

Codex again, on the uncommitted diff: FIX, one MEDIUM and two LOWs, all
taken.

- **MEDIUM: the first wording of `UNREAD` was false of five rows.** It
  said *"this app reads no rule from this row"*. `Wealth` resolves the four
  `Wealth:` rows and the builder shows their starting money, and
  `pricedVariants` takes Social Stigma's two prices out of its cell. The
  sentence now begins *"its price aside"* and claims only that nothing the
  row prints is applied. **A sentence true by construction is true of what
  the construction counts**, and `known()` counts readers of an effect.
- **LOW: a `QUIRK` note was dropped**, since the tab moved from one list
  of notes to two lists by kind. Nothing this app ships produces a quirk
  (6dp). The drawback list takes them.
- **LOW: one assertion asked `reported` what `held` should hold**, which
  checks delegation. Two expectations are stated outright beside it.

### Verification

1832 Kotlin (1283 `core:rules`, 529 `app`, 20 `core:model`), green from the

**Ten mutations of ten caught**, `ran=87` on each, launched by absolute

wrong kind and no notes, the census losing its two names, and one wrong

### Seen and not touched

- **Official Beyonder's reading is open**, and so is a language a trait

## 6er. The row the builder would not sell

6eq named this first of two successors: the builder withheld `Language
(specify)` while `language_proficiency.json` and `languages.json` sat
loaded, read only by an ungated picker in the Ritual dialog. This slice
sells a language.

### What the book prints

Lines 628-713. Twelve languages in two groups, and one three-row price
table per group: 6 / 4 / 2 for a common tongue, 30 / 20 / 10 for a mystical
one. Three sentences move a price:

- *"Points listed are for Spoken + Written at the given level.
  Spoken-only or written-only costs half."* (638-639)
- *"Language Talent halves all costs (rounded up)."* (639)
- *"Multilingual (3 pts) grants fluency in two common languages without
  point cost — it does not apply to mystical languages."* (712-713)

No language is free without Multilingual. The first check for a free native
tongue was three phrasings (`native language`, `mother tongue`, `native
tongue`), which is a keyword looking for a named thing; the final review
asked for `language|tongue|speak` over the whole book outside 628-713. It
finds no starting language either, and it finds two traits that GRANT one:
Official Beyonder's *"Hermes Language (Broken)"* (582) and Dead Language
Fluency's *"one dead language (Ancient Hermes, Ancient Loen, etc.)"*
(1059-1061).

### The design review

Codex, through `codex exec`, on a written decomposition and no diff.

- **The cost rule ships, and needs no ruling.** 6x had recorded that the two
  halvings *"interact, and the book combines them in no worked example"*,
  and 6eq inherited that as an ambiguity. It is not one. Every printed price
  is even, so the form's half is always whole, and Language Talent's
  halving then carries the only rounding the book prints. One ceiling over
  the product of the divisors gives the same numbers: 6 → 2, 2 → 1,
  30 → 8, 10 → 3 for one form with the Talent.
- **Multilingual ships as two free purchases.** *"Fluent"* is the Native
  row's own first word in both tables, and the table prices Spoken +
  Written, so the first two purchases that are common, Native and in both
  forms cost nothing. Which two is this app's convention and moves no
  total, since every eligible purchase costs the same. The review asked
  that the two be visible, and the row says *"free with Multilingual (6
  listed)"*.
- **CHANGE on the shape, twice.** A purchase composes to a `Trait` named
  `Language (Hermes, Accented)`, which `TraitEffects.catalogueName`
  resolves to the catalogue row by its placeholder rule. That rule split on
  the LAST bracket, and two printed languages carry brackets of their own:
  *Balam (Dutan)* and *Jotun (Giant's)*. It tries the last bracket and then
  the first now. And a `SavedEdits` field missing from `isEmpty` is a
  purchase that bills nothing, because `applyTo` returns the sheet
  untouched for an empty save.
- **The Ritual dialog gets a note and nothing else.** Owning a language
  does not say which one a ritual is cast in, so the picker stays ungated
  and still opens on *"Not stated"*. The note carries the form, on the
  review's LOW.

### What was built

- `Languages.owned(purchases, held)` prices, de-duplicates and names in one
  call, the shape `PurchasableTraits.resolved` takes. A language is owned
  once and the first purchase stands; a row is validated before it claims
  its language. `OwnedLanguage.costLine` is authored in rules, so the
  builder types no number of its own.
- `SavedEdits.languages`, additive and defaulted: three names and never a
  price. Languages compose LAST, so a Language Talent or Multilingual
  bought in play reprices what is already owned.
- `SavedEdits.ownedLanguages(printed)` is the one reading. The builder's
  rows, the picker's preview (`pricedWith`, which prices the candidate in
  the list it would join) and the Ritual note all ask it.
- `LanguagePicker.kt`: the twelve in the book's two groups, the three
  proficiencies at that group's prices, the three forms. Picking an owned
  language changes it in place, because position is what Multilingual's
  "first two" reads.
- `TraitEffects.UNAPPLIED` gains the language row, so a bought language is
  on the sheet with what is not applied: the *"-2 / -3 to
  language-dependent skill rolls"*, which reach nothing because the book
  tags no skill as language-dependent (6x's reason, unchanged).
- `PurchasableTraits.unoffered()` now says *"bought in the Languages row
  above"*, the sentence Wealth's row already uses.

### Potions and traits grant languages, as prose

Two blocks print *"Ancient Hermes Fluent — can speak, read, and write
this dead mystical language"* among their advantages, which are prose
(`PotionDigestion.UNPARSED`'s neighbour: advantage rows are not structure).
So the Ritual note is printed only when something was BOUGHT, and says *"A
trait or a potion may grant others"*. A line reading *"owns no mystical
language"* would have been false of those two Beyonders, and of anyone
holding either trait above.

### Tests and mutations

Seventeen tests: nine in `LanguagesTest` and eight across the three `app`
suites, plus a reworded assertion in `PurchasableTraitsTest`. Each was RED
first on an unresolved name.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| one form costs full price | *one form costs half*, and three more |
| Language Talent ignored | *Language Talent halves after the form, rounded up* |
| rounds down | the same |
| Multilingual frees a mystical language | *Multilingual frees the first two fluent common languages and nothing else* |
| …a language that is not fluent | the same |
| …one form | the same |
| …every one | the same |
| …three | the same |
| a language is owned twice | *a purchase the book does not print is dropped, and a language is owned once* |
| the form is left off the name | *every language composes to a trait the catalogue resolves* |
| the matcher splits on the last bracket only | the same |
| priced against the printed sheet only | *Language Talent bought in play halves a language already owned*, and two more |
| a re-bought language is appended | *a language is changed in place and given back by name* |
| a language-only save is empty | *a bought language reaches the composed character and its budget* |
| languages never reach the character | the same |
| giving back removes nothing | *a language is changed in place and given back by name* |

| the census cannot see the two language traits | *every trait the language prices read is one the census can see* |
| Multilingual's second clause goes unreported | the same |

Eighteen of eighteen, with the `ran=` column 6eq added and the launcher that
worked there. One equivalent mutant was written and dropped before running:
`costLine` returns early for a free language, so whether the Talent flag is
set on one cannot be observed.

1827 Kotlin (1278 `core:rules`, 529 `app`, 20 `core:model`) after
`--rerun-tasks`. The 361 Python tests were not run: no tool or content file
changed.

### The final review: two traits applied where the census could not see

`Languages.owned` read Language Talent and Multilingual through a matcher
of its own, and neither name was in any collection `TraitEffects.known()`
reads. That is the failure `VitalRollsTest` records three times, a fourth
time, and the first where the reader is another object.
`Languages.PRICING_TRAITS` is exported once and `known()` reads it; the
names are matched through `TraitEffects.levelOf`, the matcher every other
reader uses. Multilingual's cell prints a second clause, *"No penalty to
language-dependent social skills in those languages"*, which became a
clause of a handled trait the moment the first was applied (Very Fit's
precedent, 6de) and is reported now.

### The diff review

Codex returned FIX with one MEDIUM. The picker loaded an owned language's
choices from the RAW save. A hand-edited save holding `Hermes / Fluent`
ahead of `Hermes / Native` bills Native, and the picker loaded *Fluent*,
printed *"The book prints no such row"* and greyed **Change**. It reads the
resolved list now. The composition and the screen had asked two lists,
which is the failure `ownedLanguages` was written to prevent, one caller
over.

It found no state where the row, the preview, the character and the budget
disagree, and no existing sheet spelling the widened matcher resolves
differently.

### Seen and not touched

- **Official Beyonder is in no collection, no test and no slice.** A
  15-point advantage the builder sells: *"Benefits: Revolver +2,
  Ritualistic Magic +1, Hidden Lore (Beyonders) +3, Occultism +2, Hermes
  Language (Broken)"*. None of the five reaches anything and the sheet
  says nothing, because `reported` only emits what `known()` names and the
  clause guards look for the word *roll* or a *"to X"*. A grep of both
  source trees, the tools and this log for the name returned nothing
  before this slice. No premade holds it. **Ask what else is in the
  complement of `known()`.**
- **A language a potion or a trait grants is prose.** A player can buy
  Ancient Hermes beside a block that already grants it; the guide says not
  to, and the app does not stop it.
- **6eq's second successor stands**: 6dy calls the Brawling and Wrestling

- **The picker's own logic has no test** (section 6: composables are

## 6eq. The refusals in production source, re-asked

6ep named no successor. It had re-asked three rows of a journal census,
6dy's, for one reason: a refusal whose subject is THIS APP expires, and a
refusal about the book does not. This slice ran the same check where the
refusals actually live, which is production source (6cj put them there so a
sweep over Kotlin could find them).

### The query

```bash
grep -rnE '"[^"]*(this app|this engine|nothing here|no .* here|is rolled here|this dialog|this screen)[^"]*"' \
  core/rules/src/main/kotlin app/src/main/kotlin --include=*.kt
```

39 lines, less comment lines. Three are not refusals (two `require`/`error`
messages and the Drink refusal's label). The registries behind the rest are
`TraitEffects.UNAPPLIED` and `PARTLY_APPLIED`, `Equipment.UNMODELLED`,
`Pools.UNMODELLED`, `NaturalRecovery.UNMODELLED`, `Divination.UNAPPLIED`,
`ActiveDefenses.UNPAYABLE`, `PurchasableTraits.unoffered()`, and the notes
`DefenseDialog` prints.

**I first wrote "four are not refusals" and counted the builder's note
among them.** It is the sixth row below, found by checking that sentence
after the first commit. A triage line in a write-up is a claim too.

### The verdicts

| Reason as written | Query | Verdict |

| Versatile: *"every skill on a sheet is bought, so no default is rolled here"* | callers of a default: `Divination.divinationLevelFor` | **False.** Below. |
| Medical Training, *"Use Physician at IQ-2 without purchasing the skill"*: *"this app never shows an untrained level, so no default is rolled"* | the same | **False as a claim, true as a gap.** No row offers that level. Reworded. |
| Resistant: *"the one bare HT roll this app makes — a Major Wound's"* | `htRollBonus` callers and the HT rolls on screen | **Stale count.** Five now: major wound, consciousness, survival, stun recovery, daily recovery. The verdict holds and the count is gone. |
| the Retreat note: *"the GM's to count; this screen keeps no round"* | `RoundState.newRound()`, the **New round** button | **False since 6cp.** The screen keeps a round and clears Retreat on it. Which attack is the one is still the GM's. |
| First Aid: *"this app tracks a pool and no wounds, so it cannot say which wound was treated"*, and the guide's *"First Aid … not offered"* | `skills.json`, the fixtures, `TraitEffects.SKILL_BONUSES` | **The reason holds and its implication does not.** First Aid is a catalogue skill on nine premades, rolled from Skills with Healer's +3 applied. ae2f957 fixed the same sentence for Physician and missed its sibling. |

Split, below. |

| Fit, Very Fit, Unfit, Rapid Recovery: *"no clock"* | book 2838-2846, and the cell of Rapid Recovery | Hold. 6ep's split does not transfer: the FP table prints rates and no roll, and both of Rapid Recovery's halves are durations. |

### Versatile, and why the +1 is inside the pick

Book 612-615: *"+1 to defaults skill rolls — any time you use a skill at
default, you are effectively one level better."* Book 3559: *"Default:
Divination Arts defaults to Ritualistic Magic-2 and vice versa."* The book
calls the number a default in its own word, the dialog prints *"Defaulted
from"*, three premades carry Versatile and the builder sells it.

The design review (Codex, through `codex exec`) returned SHIP on the
application and gave the case that decided its shape: own 10 against a
sibling of 12. The default is 10, a tie, and a tie keeps the owned skill.
With Versatile the default is 11 and wins. Adding the +1 after the pick
rolls 10 for that caster. So `divinationLevelFor(own, sibling,
defaultBonus)` adds it before the comparison, the 12+ gate still reads the
sibling's own level, and `SkillOrDefault` carries the bonus because
`sourceLine` used to recover the sibling's level by subtracting from the
chosen number, which would have printed it one too high.

Its strongest objection was book 424-425, where a default is *"always worse
than trained use"*. It answered that itself: 3559 conditions on the source
skill and never on lacking the target.

`defaultBonus` is a required parameter on both functions, not an optional
one. 6dz is why: an optional parameter is one a caller can forget.

### What was not built

**Medical Training's Physician at IQ-2 has no row.** The review called it
*"an explicit, implementable entitlement"* and accepted a disclosed gap. It
also declined to say Versatile would lift it: *"without purchasing the
skill"* does not make it a default. The reason now reads *"the Skills tab
has no row for a level a trait grants, so this one is not offered — a gap,
not a ruling"*. No premade carries the trait.

### The language row

`Languages`' own KDoc has the real reason: *"Spoken-only or
written-only costs half"* and *"Language Talent halves all costs (rounded
up)"* interact, and the book combines them in no worked example. That is a
reason about the book. The builder printed a different one, about the app,
and shared it with Reputation, which prints *"varies"* and no table at all.
`unoffered()` now files the language row alone.

**My first rewording moved the false claim rather than removing it.** It
led with the two halvings, and a second Codex pass over the changes made
after its first returned a MEDIUM: book 638-639 states both, ordinary
purchases need neither, and a missing worked example *"does not establish
that pricing is unspecified"*. The row now reads *"buying a language is
not built yet; the Languages section prices it by proficiency, and this
app holds that table"*. Reputation's half of the old sentence went in the
same pass, on the final review: the book prints *"varies"* and no
procedure, so there was none for the app to have left unread.

**Nothing is sold by this.** A language at full proficiency with no
Language Talent is one printed number (6, 4 or 2; 30, 20 or 10). That is
the successor.

### Tests and mutations

Six tests. Five were RED first on an unresolved parameter and two
unresolved names, and the sixth on its own assertion, three times: once
for each rewording of the builder's two reasons.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| bonus added after the pick | *a bonus to defaults is counted before the better number is picked* |
| bonus opens the 12+ gate | *a bonus to defaults does not open the gate at eleven* |
| the source line recovers the sibling from the level | *the source line names the sibling's own level and the bonus* |
| the chosen level forgets its bonus | the same |
| `levelsFor` drops the bonus | *a bonus to defaults is counted…* |
| `DEFAULT(VERSATILE, 0)` | *Versatile lifts a roll made at a default* |
| the stale sentence returns under Medical Training | *no refusal says this app rolls no default* |
| the sheet's note stops naming the skill | *Versatile lifts…* |
| `DEFAULT_BONUS = 0` | *Versatile lifts…*, only after the diff review |

**The harness printed eight SURVIVED lines twice before it ran once.** A
Windows Python resolves `bash` to WSL, and `cmd /c gradlew.bat` did not
find the wrapper either, which is 6en's error to the letter. The absolute
path with `shell=True` ran it. What kept the false lines from being read as
results was a `ran=` column: the log has to contain `Task :core:rules:test`
before a survivor counts.

1809 Kotlin (1268 `core:rules`, 521 `app`, 20 `core:model`) after
`--rerun-tasks`, and 361 Python, which this slice did not touch.

## 6ep. Three refusals re-asked, and the one that was half a roll

6eo named no successor and 6ek's list was empty. The handover names one
cheap check for that state: 6dy's census of the 196 unclaimed mechanical
lines is *"a claim with an expiry date — three of its rows are refusals
whose reason is a claim about this app, and one grep per row is what
checking it costs"*. This slice ran them.

### The three rows

| Book lines | Refusal as recorded | Query | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2599-2601, Grappling ST bonus | *"needs an ST-for-grappling path and a trait (`Wrestling Master`) this app does not hold"* | every row of `unarmed_attacks.json` with an `opposedRoll`; a grep of the content files for the trait | **Holds, on a sharper reason.** The three grappling rows roll Wrestling against *"DX or Escape"* or *"DX or Wrestling"*. No roll on the book's own table reads ST, so the bonus has nothing to modify. The trait is in no content file. |
| 4398, CoR by a month's abstinence | *"refused, the clock again"* | the CoR stepper | **Holds, and the reason was the wrong one.** The CoR `−1` stepper already applies it. What the app does not hold is the month, which is the GM's. |
| 2861-2895, the recovery rates | *"they are clocks, and this app holds none"* (6dc) | the table itself, lines 2857-2900 | **Splits.** Below. |

Two neighbours were read on the way and stand. Line 4161's wrong-timing
penalty is refused for a reason about the BOOK (preparation already prices
timing), pinned by `extract_ritual.py`. Line 2375's initiative roll is
refused for *"no initiative, no map, no turn counter"*, and a grep for
`initiative` over both source trees finds comments only.

### The split

The table's first row reads *"Natural Recovery (HT roll success) — 1 HP (2
HP w/ Very Rapid Healing) — Per day; rest & food required"*, and line 2897
calls it *"the daily HT roll used for Natural Recovery"*. 6dc's reason
covers the RATE. It does not cover the roll, and this app already makes
that split: `StunRecovery` offers *"roll HT each turn"* and leaves the turn
to the GM, and the fright table's recovery rolls do the same (6dr, 6ds).
The app had no way to roll a bare HT at all, so the row reached nothing.

The player guide's *"Track a clock it does not hold"* bullet names FP
recovery, stun duration and reload rates. It never named HP. The design
review was asked whether that absence was a deliberate statement, and
answered that an omission establishes no exclusion.

### The design review: build it, and restore nothing

Codex returned **A, with explicit limits on automatic healing**. Its
strongest objection decided the shape: *"rolling and changing HP presents
an authoritative result despite unresolved scaling and unrepresented
healing abilities."* So the roll is offered and **nothing is restored by
it**. The book's rows are printed, and the HP stepper applies them. Each of
these would otherwise have been decided in silence:

- *"Natural Recovery (20–29 HP) — 2× base rate"* does not say maximum or
  current HP.
- *"scales proportionally"* prints no band past 39, and the builder reaches
  a maximum well past 100 (ST 19 and a hundred HP steps). `floor(max / 10)`
  would be an extrapolation.
- *"2 HP w/ Very Rapid Healing"* names a trait no catalogue prints. The
  phrase occurs once in the book (6dc).

Its other findings, all taken:

- **The dead are not offered the roll.** My draft showed the row whenever
  HP was below maximum, which includes *"Dead — no roll required"*.
- **The result is not keyed on the target**, unlike `VitalRollRow`. The HP a
  success restores can lift the pool penalty, and the result has to outlive
  the taps that apply it. It prints the target it was rolled against.
- **The row prints all three cells**, so *"rest & food required"* is on
  screen.

### Rapid Healing has no carrier

*"Rapid Healing +5 to daily HT rolls to recover HP"* (6928-6930) is granted
by Chained Sequence 8 and by nothing else: a search of both pathway
catalogues and `advantages.json` for `Rapid Healing|daily HT|Regenerat|Very
Rapid` finds that one grant, Chained 7 and 6's Regeneration, and two
abilities that use the word (Moon 9, Everlasting 9). A potion's advantages
are prose, so no `Trait` holds the
+5. Matching it out of prose at roll time is the parser-in-the-engine this
repo refuses.

**The 23 premades were searched too, after the final review asked which
corpus the claim was checked against.** `advantages.json` holds none of
these traits, so the builder cannot sell one, and that leaves a printed
sheet as the only other way a character could hold a real `Trait`. A grep
of `fixtures/*.json` for `Healing|Regenerat` returns nothing. So "no
carrier" and two of `UNMODELLED`'s four reasons hold on all three corpora.

So the row carries a `−1 / +1` modifier, unbounded as the Fright dialog's
is, and says what it is for. The first wording was wrong, and the diff
review caught it: *"none is applied for you"* sat beside a target that DOES
include the all-HT-roll traits, which invites entering Fit twice. It now
reads *"Only what the line above shows is applied for you"*, under the
line that shows it.

### What was built

- `tools/extract_recovery.py` reads lines 2860-2868 as three three-cell
  rows into `hp_recovery.json`, verbatim. It refuses a cell count that is
  not a multiple of three, and pins the three method names, so a widened
  range fails.
- `ContentLoader.hpRecovery()` and `HpRecoveryRow`.
- `NaturalRecovery`: `isOffered(hp)`, `bonusFor(traits)` (the all-HT-roll
  traits, NOT `VitalRolls.bonusFor`, whose two bonuses are scoped to death
  and consciousness), `targetFor(ht, traits, poolPenalty, gmModifier)`, and
  `UNMODELLED`: First Aid, Physician, the Healing advantage and
  Regeneration, each with its own reason. Only the last is a clock.
- `RecoveryRollRow` under the HP row in the Vitals tab.

### Tests, mutations, and two functions with no caller

Four Python tests and six Kotlin ones, each failing first (an unresolved
import, an unresolved object).

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| offered to the dead | *the roll is offered to a hurt character who is not dead* |
| offered at full HP | the same |
| takes the death-roll bonus | *the bonuses scoped to the two threshold rolls stay with them* |
| drops the GM modifier | *the target is HT, the pool penalty and what the GM adds* |
| drops the pool penalty | the same |
| drops the traits | *a trait that reaches every HT roll reaches this one* |
| two more, on `rollRow` and `largerBodies` | caught, and then both functions were deleted |

**`rollRow()` and `largerBodies()` were written, tested, mutated and
called by nothing.** The composable prints `rows()` whole. That is 6cf's
class, a tested function with no caller, in code an hour old. Both are
gone, with their assertions.

Codex returned **FIX** with three findings.

- **MEDIUM, taken.** The *"none is applied"* wording, above.
- **LOW, taken.** *"The table's other four methods"* was three. Regeneration

## 6eo. The purchase on one screen, the character on the next

6en left one of 6ek's items standing: *"The builder prints bought values
without potion grants. Before this slice it showed HP `0` beside a sheet
reading `2 / 2`. Pre-existing."* Checked before it was believed, on the
SM-T570: Antiquarian Dealer, Abyss Sequence 9 at 100%, read `HP 11 / 11` on
the sheet's Vitals tab and `HP 9`, `ST 9`, `Will 10`, `Per 10` in the
builder. Abyss 9 grants ST +2, Will −1 and Per +2.

The cause was one line. The builder drew every number from
`Derive.of(character)`, the PURCHASED character, which is the right source
for the budget and the wrong one for a number the player reads as their
score. The weapons row on the same screen had already been moved to the
digested levels for this reason; `liveSkillLevels`' KDoc records it.

### What changed, and what did not

- **Attribute and secondary rows show the value as played**, the number the
  sheet shows. Where a potion moved it, the small line appends *"N before
  potions"*. A mortal, and a row no potion touched, print what they printed
  before.
- **Everything stepped, priced, bounded or refused stays on the purchase.**
  In `AttributeRow`, `level` feeds six things: *"pts spent here"*, *"next
  level costs"*, *"sheet prints"*, `> BASE_ATTRIBUTE`, `< ceiling` and
  `onChange`. Only the big number has a new source, through a new `played`
  parameter and not a repointed `level`. `SecondaryRow` takes the bought
  label beside the played one; its steps were already the save's.
- **One reading.** `Character.digestedWith(state)` in `EditedCharacter.kt`
  replaces four inline `PotionDigestion.of(x.copy(beyonder = …), …)` calls:
  the sheet's vitals and attributes, `shortfallOn` and `corCeilingOn`. The
  builder is the fifth caller. `MainActivity` no longer imports
  `PotionDigestion`.
- **The label is a pure function**, `beforePotions(bought, played)`, null
  when the two agree.

### Why both numbers

The builder's `−` can be greyed by a floor on EITHER score, and that
decided the design. Under Abyss, HP bought to 1 plays as 3 and `−` is
greyed by the bought floor. Will bought to 2 plays as 1 and `−` is greyed by
the digested ceiling. Either number alone leaves a greyed control beside a
value that is not at its floor. With both on the row, each floor has its
number.

The played value is the big one because it is the one the sheet prints, and
because the secondary row's small line already carried the purchase
(*"−8 bought"*).

### Skills: labelled, not re-levelled

The skill rows stay on bought levels. My draft left them unlabelled and
recorded the omission; **the design review's MEDIUM was that an unlabelled
"level 12" acquires a false meaning** beside attributes now shown as
played. For a Beyonder each row now reads *"8 pts - level 12 before
potions"*, and its study line is headed *"Study (before potions):"*.

**The first build labelled only half of that.** The words were appended to
a study DESTINATION (*"→ level 13"*), and every study line on the tablet
was a refusal: *"Study alone cannot pass 11, and this skill is already
12."* That names a bought level too, and carried no label. The final
review caught it from this slice's own device dump. The label now sits on
the line's heading, which both branches share.

They are not re-levelled here for a reason in `PotionDigestion.digest`: a
potion either lifts a bought skill with its attribute or supersedes it with
a grant, and the grant's key can differ from the purchase's, because the
match ignores the controlling attribute. Finding the played level of a
bought row would take a second matcher on this screen. The sheet prints the
levels actually rolled.

### Declined

**The design review's other MEDIUM: a printed reason for each refused
`−`.** Its point is fair, that *"N before potions"* explains the difference
and not the refusal. But `allows` answers yes or no, five different bounds
can refuse a step, and a reason per bound is a second slice. Both numbers
are now beside the control, which is what this slice set out to print.

Its LOW asked whether digestion can throw in composition. It cannot for a
character the builder holds: the opening repair and `allows` keep every
save inside the floors (6ek) and ceilings (6el), and the weapons row
already digests in composition on this screen.

### Tests and mutations

Two tests were written first and failed on unresolved references:
`digestedWith` on Abyss 9 (ST 11, HP 11, Will 9; null for a mortal), and
`beforePotions` in both directions and when nothing moved.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| the note is never printed | *a number a potion moved…* |
| the note's condition inverted | the same |
| the note names the played number | the same |
| `digestedWith` ignores the potions drunk | *the builder reads the character the sheet plays*, and four session tests through `shortfallOn` and `corCeilingOn` |

**The call sites have no test and are refused one** (section 6, and 6ej's
precedent). Printing `level` where the row prints `played` was run as a
mutation and survives the suite (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`). The device pass
below is what covers them.

`--rerun-tasks`, and 357 Python.

- **The diff review returned SHIP with no findings.** It listed thirteen

## 6en. Two rows the floors did not reach

6em left two of 6ek's items standing. This is the first: *"Selling a
secondary refunds points without limit. With Basic Speed and Basic Move at
−100 the budget bar read `-808 of 100 points, 908 spare`… Whether a reduced
secondary counts against chapter 3's '-40 points of disadvantages' (book
line 1120) is a question for the book, and it was not asked here."*

### The book, asked

- Lines 353-386 price every secondary *"±N pts per level"* (Speed *"±5 pts
  per 0.25"*) and print no floor and no cap.
- Line 1120 states the cap of *"disadvantages"*, and 455-456 as *"Take
  Disadvantages… up to -40 pts worth"*. The chapter then lists them.
- A grep over the whole book for `minimum|at least|no less|cannot
  (fall|go|drop)|to 0|below` within 60 characters of `move` or `speed`
  returned nothing. The only in-play reductions are effects on a target
  (*"-1 Basic Speed, -1 Basic Move for 1d6 turns"*, 6886-6887), which this
  app does not model.

So the book answers neither question. Both answers below are the app's, and
each is labelled so in the source.

### Two floors, on a warrant of their own

`ScoreFloors`' KDoc gives its reason as *"the lowest values the rules this
app models can compute on"*. That reason does not hold for these rows: 6ek's
own census, on the tablet, showed Vitals, Defend, Attack and Damage all open
at Speed −20.50 and Move −100. A floor added under that sentence would have
borrowed a warrant that does not apply. `MIN_MOVE = 0` and
`MIN_SPEED_QUARTERS = 0` carry their own, labelled policy:

- **Move is a distance.** *"How far you move per second"* (172), *"Move up to
  your full Basic Move in meters"* (2391). Below 0 it names none.
- **Speed is held because Move alone bounds nothing.** Speed sold a hundred
  quarters refunds 500 and drags Move's base to −21; Move bought back 21
  costs 105. That is 395 points kept with Move standing at a legal 0.
- **Zero, not lower.** My draft gave the book's two roundings as the reason
  for the floor: *"rounded down"* (382) against *"drop fractions"* (172,
  2464). The design review's one finding was that this does not establish a
  minimum, since a negative INTEGER satisfies both. The KDoc now says only
  that the two part company on a negative fraction, as a reason for zero
  rather than for the floor.

What the pair can still refund is 5 × (HT + DX) points: 90 at the book's 9s,
since Move's base is 0 once Speed is.

### One function changed

`ScoreFloors.shortfall` returns two more rows. `allows`, `canSetAttribute`,
`canSetSecondary` and the opening repair already read it, and `boughtBack`
folds over every priced key, so **no session or screen code changed**. The
builder greys `−` on both rows, and on DX and HT when a step would take
Speed below zero.

**Move's row is measured after Speed's repair.** Move's base is Speed
rounded down, so buying Speed back returns part of Move. Read in one pass, a
save at −100 / −100 with attributes of 9 stands at Speed −82 quarters and
Move −121, and owes Move 121 steps. A `SecondaryDelta` holds ±100, so the
repair meant to rescue that save would have thrown in its constructor.
Measured after, it owes 82 quarters and 100 steps, and opens at
`basicSpeed = -18` with no Move purchase left.

No potion lowers either row. `ScoreFloorsTest`'s *no potion lowers anything
but Will* reads every `stats` row of both catalogues, so the two-pass bound
in the opening repair still holds, and a floor on the bought score is
enough.

### The −40, refused as a reading

A sold secondary is not counted against the disadvantage cap. The reason is
in `PointBudget`'s KDoc, in production source, and it is worded as a reading
and not a quotation: the book states the cap of a category it goes on to
list, and prices secondaries with no cap of their own. Nothing printed files
a sold level under either heading. GURPS Basic counts it, and `ScoreFloors`
already records that GURPS Basic's limits are not borrowed. The design
review called the reading defensible and asked that it be documented as an
interpretation, which is how it is written.

### Tests and mutations

Five tests were written first and failed for the stated reason: two in
`ScoreFloorsTest` (the floors themselves; Move after Speed) and three in
`BeyonderSessionTest` (the setters refuse; DX `−` is refused at Speed 0; a
−100 / −100 save opens at `basicSpeed = -18` and is written back).

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| no Speed floor | both `ScoreFloorsTest` cases, the repair test, and *…are not sold below zero* **after an assertion was added** |
| no Move floor | all four |
| Move not measured after Speed | both `ScoreFloorsTest` cases and the repair test |
| `MIN_MOVE = -1` | all four |
| `MIN_SPEED_QUARTERS = -1` | both `ScoreFloorsTest` cases and the repair test |
| the returned Move ignores the old base | all four |

**The first run reported six survivors, and none was one.** The harness
called `gradlew.bat` through `cmd /c` without `.\`, which is not found;
every run exited 1 and named no failing test, and the script read "exit 1,
no test named, no `e:` line" as a survival. It now asserts a success token
(`tests completed` or `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`) before it reads anything. That is
the failure-filter-cannot-see-a-no-op class, in a script an hour old.

The session tests at first caught the missing Speed floor only through
Move: Speed −19 drags Move to −1, and the Move floor refuses. An assertion
was added that separates them — Move bought `+1` on top, where Move stands
at 0 and only Speed's own floor refuses — and the mutation was re-run
against it.

## 6em. A state the app only checked on the way in

6el named no successor, and 6ek had left three items. This is the first:
*"an edit that lowers a POSITIVE ceiling onto the CoR total does not latch
the loss; the next CoR gain does."* Checked before it was believed, it is
worse than that sentence says.

The book prints the rule as a STATE: *"Maximum CoR equals the character's
Will score. Reaching maximum CoR means the character becomes an NPC monster
… removed from play"* (book lines 3059-3060), and *"[!] At maximum CoR: The
character is permanently lost"* (3075). The app latched it only inside
`gainCor`. Three builder edits lower the ceiling without a gain: selling Will
steps, selling IQ (Will = IQ + steps), and selling a bought Spiritual
Fortitude (+3, line 1028). So a character at CoR 9 under Will 10 could sell
one Will and stand at 9 / 9, live. **And the next gain does not always latch
it**: a CoR `−1` tap there is `isLostAfter(9, −1, 9)` = `isLostAt(8, 9)`,
false. So the stepper walked the character back out, and the book's
"permanently" was never reached. The design review found that, against my
draft's claim that leaving old saves alone was safe.

### Refuse, not latch: the split the code already makes

The strongest case for latching on the edit is the book's own wording, plus
a precedent: a potion that lowers Will onto the total is warned about before
the tap (`drinkLine`) and latched by `drink`. The design review made that
case and then ruled against it **by role**. A potion is an event in the book;
selling Will in play is app latitude, since the book prints no such sale.
Where only an app bound is at stake, this repo already refuses rather than
latches: 6ek's `holdsCeiling` refusal on Drink, and `ScoreFloors`. So:

- **A builder edit is refused** when it would leave a live character at or
  above the ceiling. `BeyonderSession.allows` asks
  `keepsBelowCeiling(next)`, after the floors, because a candidate below a
  floor may not digest. The builder greys `−` through `canSet*` as before,
  and the trait row's *Give back* is now greyed through a new `canSellTrait`,
  with the line *"Kept: giving it back would bring maximum CoR to the CoR
  total or below 1."* Before this, a refused sale was a button that did
  nothing.
- **A save already at or past its ceiling buys Will back once on opening**,
  to one above the total, and writes back. It runs after 6el's ceilings and
  6ek's floors. Buying Will only raises the ceiling, so no floor moves. Only
  if the purchase ceiling (Will +98) stops the buy-back short does the
  character stand at maximum and is lost. That is the book's answer, and the
  latch is persisted even though the edits did not change.
- **The first potion latches now.** `drink`'s mortal branch set the state
  and returned without `gainCor(0, ceilingAfter)`. A mortal can carry CoR (a
  ritual's), and Abyss Sequence 9 is Will −1. Before this slice that left
  one loss unlatched. After it, the opening repair would have bought the
  loss back with a Will purchase. The diff review's MEDIUM.

The ceiling now has **one reading**, `SavedEdits.corCeilingOn(sheet,
state)`. The session, the sheet screen's `maxCor` and the pathway screen's
`maxCorFor` all ask it; before, two screens composed it separately. The
review traced both old paths and found no number changes. ScoreFloors' Will
row is a third computation, and it is left alone because it answers a floor
question.

**And a label was false.** The tracker printed *"maximum CoR is Will
($max)"*, and on the tablet under Fortitude it read *"Will (13)"* beside a
Will of 10. It now prints the number alone. That is the
"literal restating a computed number" class; a grep found no other copy.

### Tests and mutations

The RED test was written to hold under either design: after each of the
three edits, `isLost || cor < ceiling`. It failed with *"CoR 9 under a
ceiling of 9, and live"*. The tests after the design review failed on an
unresolved `canSellTrait`, and the first-potion test on `isLost` false.
One of my own tests was wrong, not the code: the Beyonder case first used
CoR 7, where selling one Will leaves 7 / 8, which is legal. At CoR 8 it
separates the digested ceiling (8 / 8, refused) from the undigested one
(8 / 9).

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `allows` skips the ceiling | the boundary test, the three-edit test, the Fortitude test |
| `>` → `>=` | the boundary test, the three-edit test |
| no buy-back on opening | *a save already standing at its ceiling…* |
| `canSellTrait` skips `allows` | the Fortitude test |
| no latch when the buy-back falls short | *…cannot buy back above its total is lost* |
| latch persisted only when edits change | the same, **after retargeting it** |
| ceiling read without the potions drunk | the first-potion test and *a Beyonder's ceiling…* |
| buy-back ignores `isLost` | *a lost save is not bought back*, the first-potion test |
| first potion does not latch | the first-potion test |

The persistence mutation first **survived** (exit 0). The test started at
IQ 30, so `withinCeilings` changed the edits, and the save was written
anyway. It now starts at both purchase ceilings (IQ 26, Will +98, CoR 124),
so the edits come back unchanged and only the latch can trigger the write.
One run was a **compile failure, not a survival**: the mutation text
contained `||`, the harness's own pair separator. That is the reason 6eh
gives for reading `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` and the testcase, not the exit code.
