  refunds without limit, and the builder prints bought values without potion
  grants.
- **An old save at the ceiling is repaired at a cost of points, and nothing
  says why.** That is the same trade 6ek recorded for the floors, made for
  the same reason.

## 6el. The ceiling a browse could cross

6ek named its successor as the ceiling side of its own overflow:
`PotionDigestion.kt:206-215` adds a potion's grants to the bought score, and
the sum goes through the `Attributes` (9..30) and `SecondaryDelta` (±100)
constructors, which throw. Its two examples were *"HP +100 with any HP
grant, or ST 29–30 with Abyss Sequence 8's ST +2"*. The first names nothing.
**No standard block grants HP or FP**; Abyss's +2 HP comes through ST, which
is what HP is built from. And the successor's frame — the potion this
character DRINKS — is the narrow half.

### The census, and the wider path

Every walk of `pathways.json` (22 pathways × Seq 9–6), cumulative, at its
peak:

| Row | Largest walk | Pathway |
|---|---|---|
| ST | +11 | Twilight Giant |
| HT | +5 | Twilight Giant |
| DX | +4 | Demoness, Moon |
| IQ | +4 | White Tower |
| Will, Per, Basic Move | +2 | several |
| Basic Speed | +4 quarters | Moon |
| HP, FP | none | — |

Only Abyss lowers anything (Will, −4 by Seq 6). No premade prints a
secondary delta, and the highest printed attribute is 11. The 17
non-standard blocks are displayed by the Boon dialog and never digested.

**`PathwayScreen.kt:122-126` digests the BROWSED block while it draws**, not
the drunk one. So a character who bought ST 20 — any character, a mortal
included — crashed the pathway screen by tapping Twilight Giant, then Seq 6.
No potion and no Drink were involved. Reproduced on the SM-T570 on the
pre-fix build: Academic Researcher (Fool Seq 9), ST bought to 20 (20,470
points), Twilight Giant, Seq 6, and the process died with
`IllegalArgumentException: ST must be between 9 and 30 … was 31` at
`PotionDigestion.kt:206`. A check scoped to a BeyonderState — the shape 6ek's
floors take — cannot reach that path. Only a bound that holds for every walk
can.

### What shipped

- **`PurchaseCeilings`** (core:rules). Each bound less the largest cumulative
  grant on any walk: ST 19, DX 26, IQ 26, HT 25; Will, Per and Basic Move 98
  steps, Basic Speed 96 quarters, HP and FP 100. It is DERIVED from
  `ContentLoader.pathways()` through `PotionDigestion.largestGrants`, which
  folds each walk with the same `statGrants`/`mergeStats` digestion uses and
  takes each row's peak at every Sequence. Each row is maximised on its own,
  because each constructor checks each field on its own. A `ponytail:`
  comment records it as the app's bound, not the book's.
- **`SavedEdits.withinCeilings()`**, the one statement of the range: each
  bought attribute in 9..ceiling, each bought secondary in −100..ceiling.
  `setAttribute` and `setSecondary` build through it, and so does
  `BeyonderSession`'s opening repair. The repair runs BEFORE 6ek's floor pass
  and is written back.
- **The builder** greys `+` at the ceiling, and its *"next level costs"* label
  stops at the same number.

ST 19 already costs 10,230 points against characters built on about 100, so
the cap takes nothing a legal character holds.

### The design review, and why the alternative lost

Codex was rate-limited (reset 15:26) and the 9router gateway refused the
probe (`fetch failed`), so both reviews went to one general-purpose
sub-agent, scoped to three questions with "do not read CLAUDE.md or
docs/SLICE-LOG.md".

Asked for the strongest case AGAINST a purchase cap, it made one: the
attribute bound's own KDoc says it exists because `AttributeCosts`'s doubling
ladder overflows, and digested scores are never priced. So the bound
arguably belongs on purchases only, and a cap takes ST 20–30 from a Fool
because of a walk the Fool will never take. **Then it found what kills that
option**: ST has a second reader with the same ceiling. `Damage.rowFor`
errors outside `thrust_swing.json`, which runs ST 1..30, and
`MainActivity.kt:316-320` feeds it the DIGESTED ST. An unbounded effective
type would only move the ST 31 crash from digestion to the damage dialog.

It changed three things:

1. **One ceiling function**, read by both setters, both builder controls and
   the repair. My draft had a third copy in `SessionStore.load`.
2. **The repair goes in `init`, not `load`.** `load` does not write back, a
   test-built session bypasses it, and it would have been the third copy of
   the bound. Order matters: lowering ST lowers HP (ST + steps), so the
   ceiling must be applied before the floors are asked.
3. **Pin the second reader**: the at-every-ceiling test rolls
   `Damage.thrust` on each digested ST.

It also named a digest site my census had missed, `liveSkillLevels`
(`EditedCharacter.kt:199-201`). It reads the drunk state and is covered by
the same cap.

### Tests and mutations

RED first in both modules. In app, a fix-agnostic reproduction (*"whatever
the builder sells, every potion can be digested on top of it"*) failed with
the device's own exception. The opening-repair test (*"…brought down to it
on opening, before the floors"*) failed on its expected edits. In
core:rules, `PurchaseCeilingsTest` did not compile. Then GREEN.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| no ceiling in `init` | the opening-repair test |
| ceilings applied after the floor pass | the opening-repair test (HP −20 kept, sheet HP −1) |
| `setAttribute` holds to 30 only | the reproduction, **after a fix to the test** |
| `setSecondary` holds to ±100 only | the reproduction |
| `largestGrants` reads the walk's END, not its peak | *a walk is measured at its peak* — **after a new test** |
| `atLeast` keeps the later pathway, not the max | all three census tests |
| secondary ceiling ignores the grants | the literal pin and the at-every-ceiling test |
| attribute ceiling one too strict | the tightness test and the literal pin |

Two of those first SURVIVED, and both were test gaps:

- **The `setAttribute` mutation survived** because the test bought
  attributes and then secondaries on one session. `withinCeilings()` holds
  the WHOLE save, so the secondary steps clamped the ST the attribute setter
  had let through. Each setter now runs on its own session.
- **The peak-versus-end mutation survived** because no standard walk lowers
  a row after raising it. Abyss lowers Will, and Black Emperor's +2 dominates
  that row anyway. `largestGrants` takes its blocks as a parameter, so a
  two-block synthetic walk (ST +3, then −1) now separates the two.

The diff review returned SHIP with four LOWs. Three were taken:

- the tightness helper counted ANY throw as "over the ceiling", and now
  rethrows anything that is not a bound on the sum;
- its key list was hard-coded, and is now every row whose ceiling is under
  100, pinned as a set;
- a printed attribute (a null edit) is never held, so a test pins every
  premade's printed attributes under the ceilings.

The fourth asked for a guard that a ceiling stays ≥ 9. It was declined
because the literal pin (ST 19 …) already fails first.

Tests: 1782 Kotlin (1254 `core:rules`, 508 `app`, 20 `core:model`) after
`--rerun-tasks`, and 357 Python.

### On the SM-T570

| Build | State | Screen |
|---|---|---|
| before | ST bought to 20, Twilight Giant → Seq 6 | crash, `PotionDigestion.kt:206`, `was 31` |
| after | the same save, opened | builder reads ST 19, `10230 pts spent here`, no "next level costs" |
| after | ST `+` | `enabled=false`; DX/IQ/HT and every secondary `+` live; a tap leaves 19 |
| after | Twilight Giant → Seq 6 | *Sequence 6: Dawn Paladin* renders; crash buffer empty |

The premade was left as found: ST 9, Fool Sequence 9, 0%, 0 CoR, *"1 of 17
values differ"*. Not exercised on the device: a Drink, and the secondary
ceilings, which are covered by the unit tests only.

### Seen and not touched

- **SPI is the same sum on a row no purchase reaches, and it is clear.** The
  largest walk is SPI +22 (Wheel of Fortune), the highest printed SPI is 9,
  and `Character.spi` is bounded at `MAX_SPI` = 1000; `effectiveSpi` is a
  plain `Int` that no reader puts back into a `Character`.
- **Two bounds' own words had expired**, and were reworded in the same
  commit as this entry: `MAX_ATTRIBUTE` called itself a purchase bound that
  nothing came close to, and `SecondaryDelta` called ±100 well clear of any
  delta. Bought ST 19 on Twilight Giant's walk is a legal ST 30. The
  substrings `must be between` and `magnitude too large` are kept, because
  the tightness test keys on them.
- **The ceiling is derived from content, so a re-extraction that raises a
  grant lowers it**, and the next open clips a save bought to the old
  ceiling. That is deliberate: the alternative is a crash. The literal pin
  will fail first and name the row.
- **6ek's three remaining items stand**: a positive ceiling lowered onto the
  CoR total does not latch; selling Basic Speed and Basic Move refunds
  without limit; the builder prints bought values without potion grants.

## 6ek. Four floors the builder could sell through

6ej named its successor: *"every CoR-gaining TAP on such a character still
throws"*. That was about a Will bought below 1. Checked before it was
believed, it is true, and it is the smallest of four. The builder's `−` on
every priced secondary runs to `-MAX_SECONDARY_DELTA_MAGNITUDE`, a hundred
steps, which 6ej had already called an overflow bound and not a rule. Four
guards in `core:rules` throw below a value the builder could sell past:

| Guard | Throws below |
|---|---|
| `Pools.requireMax` (`Pools.hp`, `Pools.fp`) | an HP or FP maximum of 1 |
| `Wounds` (`majorWoundThreshold`, `effectsAt`) | an HP maximum of 1 |
| `Corruption.requireWillScore` | a CoR ceiling of 1 |
| `Detection` | a Per of 0 |

**The HP check runs while the screen is drawn, not on a tap.** Reproduced on
the SM-T570 with Antiquarian Dealer: ST 9, Abyss Sequence 9 (which grants +2
HP). HP sold nine steps read `HP 2 / 2`. At eleven steps, opening the sheet
killed the app with `IllegalArgumentException: HP max must be at least 1; was
0` at `MainActivity.kt:374`, in `SheetScreen`'s composition. The save kept the
number, so that premade crashed on every open. The builder is reached from the
sheet, so no tap could undo it.

### What the book says, and what else writes a score

The book prints no floor. Chapter 2's table (book lines 353-386) prices each
row `±N pts per level` and says nothing more. GURPS Basic's limits are not
this book's, and none is borrowed. So the floors are the app's: the lowest
values the rules it models can compute on. `ScoreFloors` says so in a
`ponytail:` comment.

The writers, each checked rather than assumed:

- **The builder's `−` on a secondary, and on an attribute.** Will and Per are
  IQ plus what was bought, HP is ST plus what was bought, and FP is HT plus
  what was bought.
- **Selling a bought Spiritual Fortitude.** "Maximum CoR equal Will + 3"
  (book line 1028), so the ceiling can drop by three with no stepper touched.
  The design review found this one.
- **Drink.** Of the 88 + 17 potion blocks, the only negative grants are
  Abyss's Will −1, −1 and −2 (Sequences 9, 8 and 6). A mortal at Will 1 who
  drinks Abyss Sequence 9 lands at a ceiling of 0. So half of 6ej's *"the
  builder's bound is where it is answered"* has expired: no builder floor
  reaches a potion.
- **A save written before this slice**, such as the tablet's own.

Not writers: `Derive` reads no trait for a secondary, and the fright table's
"Permanent loss of −1 IQ and −1 Will" (book line 2989) is text the app prints
and applies nowhere.

### What shipped

- **`ScoreFloors`.** Three constants: `MIN_POOL_MAX = 1`,
  `MIN_COR_CEILING = 1` and `MIN_PER = 0`. The four guards above read them,
  so the builder and the engine cannot disagree. It also has
  `holdsCeiling(ceiling)`, and `shortfall(secondaries, traits)`, which gives
  the steps each row needs back. The Will row is measured on the CoR CEILING.
- **`SavedEdits.shortfallOn(sheet, state)`.** The shortfall of the BOUGHT
  scores. When there is none, the shortfall of the scores with `state`'s
  potions digested.
- **`BeyonderSession(saved, sheet, onChange)`.** `setAttribute`,
  `setSecondary` and `sellTrait` all go through one `edit`, which refuses an
  edit that leaves a shortfall. `canSetAttribute` and `canSetSecondary` ask
  the same question of the same candidate the setter builds. On opening, a
  save below a floor is bought back to it and written back.
- **`drink` refuses a ceiling below 1 BEFORE it rolls or moves any state**,
  including on the first potion. The button is disabled. `drinkLine` is now
  nullable, because a mortal's first potion prints nothing unless it is
  refused, and it says *"CoR ceiling after this potion would be 0, and this
  app keeps it at 1 or more — it cannot be drunk until the ceiling is
  raised"*.
- **The builder greys `−`** on an attribute or a secondary the session would
  refuse. The trait list's remove is NOT greyed: the setter refuses it, and
  the tap does nothing.

`MainActivity` passes the selected premade into the session. That line is
the call site, and it has no test (section 6).

### The design review, before any code

Run through `codex exec` with the three questions and "do not read CLAUDE.md
or docs/SLICE-LOG.md". It changed three things:

1. **Repair once, not on every read.** I had proposed lifting the bought
   steps inside `characterFor`. Its strongest objection was two purchase
   records. The builder's label and its next step read the raw save, while
   the bill would read the lifted one, and a later potion could shrink the
   lift and hand a refund back. The precedent was already in this repo:
   `SessionStore.load` drops forbidden purchases at the boundary for the same
   reason.
2. **Spiritual Fortitude is a writer**, and the Will row is measured on the
   ceiling, not on Will.
3. **Check before anything changes, and on the first potion too.** `drink`'s
   mortal branch persists immediately, and `drinkLine` was drawn only for
   `drunk != null`.

Its strongest case AGAINST refusing Drink: the book's arithmetic already
describes the outcome (max CoR = Will, and reaching it is the end), so
refusing forbids a choice instead of showing its result. I refused anyway,
because `Corruption`'s contract rejects a non-positive ceiling, and giving it
terminal handling is a larger change than the crash warrants. It is recorded
as the app's bound, not the book's.

### Two defects in my own diff

**The first build crashed the builder on the tablet.** The screen built its
own candidate, `edits.withAttribute(attr, level - 1)`, and so asked about ST 8
when ST stood at the book's floor of 9. `Attributes` throws on an 8, during
composition. The setter coerces first; the question did not. Fixed by
`canSetAttribute` and `canSetSecondary`, which build the candidate exactly as
the setter does. The regression test's mutation fails with the device's own
exception. The same mismatch was the diff review's question 2, asked before I
found it.

**The diff review's HIGH: the repair could not repair the save it was for.**
Will −100 bought, on Abyss Sequence 9, becomes `SecondaryDelta(will = -101)`
inside `PotionDigestion`, whose constructor throws, inside the repair. Fixed
by holding the floors on the bought scores first and on the digested ones
after, and by repairing in passes. Two passes at most are needed, because a
potion lowers only Will, and by four at most. **That moves a line**: a floor
now holds on the bought score too, so HP cannot be sold to a bought 0 even
under a +2 grant. The builder can therefore no longer print a negative HP; it
had shown `-1` beside a sheet reading `1 / 1`.

### Tests and mutations

RED first in both modules (an unresolved `ScoreFloors`, unresolved `canSet*`
and a missing constructor parameter), then GREEN. Eleven single mutations
were run, each restored from a copy afterwards. Each was caught by the test
aimed at it, named from the JUnit XML: `-q` prints no test names, and a
failing exit code alone is also what a file lock looks like.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| the Will row ignores traits | *the Will floor is a CoR ceiling, so Spiritual Fortitude moves it* |
| no repair on opening | *a save already below a floor is bought back…* |
| the repair is not written back | the same |
| `edit` skips the check | *a step that would leave HP below one…*, the IQ test and the Fortitude test |
| `sellTrait` bypasses `edit` | *selling Spiritual Fortitude is refused…* |
| Drink checks advancements only | *Drink is refused before the roll…* |
| a refused first potion prints nothing | *a first potion prints nothing unless it is refused* |
| the shortfall ignores the potion | *a save already below a floor…* |
| `canSetAttribute` skips the coercion | *the builder's question is asked of the edit the setter would make* |
| digested scores checked before bought ones | both repair tests |
| one repair pass | both repair tests |

`ScoreFloorsTest` also pins the census: *no potion lowers anything but Will*.
If a block ever lowers HP, FP, Per or an attribute, Drink needs the whole
shortfall and not one row of it.

Tests: 1775 Kotlin (1249 `core:rules`, 506 `app`, 20 `core:model`) after
`--rerun-tasks`, and 357 Python.

| State | Screen |

| before the fix, HP −11 bought | sheet: crash at `MainActivity.kt:374` on every open |
| after the fix, the same save | opens; repaired and written back |
| builder, HP at the floor | `−` reads `enabled=false`; eleven taps stop at `−8 bought`, value `1`; sheet `HP 3 / 3` |
| builder, ST/DX/HT at 9 | `−` disabled; IQ 10 `−` live |
| Will −8 bought (ceiling 1), Abyss Seq 8 block | `Drink and roll` `enabled=false`, with the line *"…would be 0…cannot be drunk until the ceiling is raised"* |

The premade was left as it was found: Sequence 9 Abyss at 100%, 0 CoR,
`87 of 100 points`. Not exercised: a tap on a refused Drink.

### After the commit: is "four" a count, and what the repair costs

**"Four guards" came from a keyword-filtered grep.** It read `require(` lines
for max/per/will/hp/fp/pool and could not see three other shapes: a guard
that names only Dodge, Speed or Move; a `coerceIn(a, b)` whose upper bound is
a derived score (the shape `Corruption.clamp` has); and a division by a
derived score. Re-run wider over `core/rules/src/main` and `app/src/main`:

- `require(|check(|error(` filtered for `dodge|move|speed|quarter` — one hit,
  `PotionDigestion.kt:330`, which checks a GRANT's quarters, not a score.
- every `coerceIn(` — eleven hits; the only one bounded by a derived score is
  `Corruption.clamp`, already a floor.
- every `floorDiv(` and `/ <variable>` — all the divisors are constants.

On the tablet, with Basic Speed and Basic Move both sold to the −100 bound
(`-20.50`, `-100`), Vitals, Defend, Attack and Damage all opened with an empty
crash buffer. Both rows were then bought back, and the premade is at
`87 of 100` again. **So "four" holds for crashes**, and that is the query that
backs it.

**The repair reprices saves that rendered correctly.** The floor holds on the
BOUGHT score as well as the digested one. So a save written before this slice
on Abyss Sequence 9 (+2 HP) with HP bought −9 — a bought 0 and a digested 2,
which never crashed — is repaired to −8 on opening. That costs 2 points, and
nothing on screen says why. The design review had asked for the changed
purchases and the budget to be reported, and the original kept for recovery.
**That was declined**, as more machinery than a repair of a few points
warrants, and because no save this repair can reach was legal under 6ek's own
floors. A narrow post-commit `codex exec` over `shortfallOn` and the `init`
repair at `8946153` returned no further findings. It left unverified the
two-pass bound, which rests on the potion census `ScoreFloorsTest` pins.

### Seen and not touched

- **The ceiling side of the same overflow.** `PotionDigestion.kt:206-215`
  adds the bought delta to the grants through the `SecondaryDelta` and
  `Attributes` constructors, which throw past ±100 and past `MAX_ATTRIBUTE`
  (30). The builder lets the + side go as far as the − side used to. HP +100
  with any HP grant, or ST 29–30 with Abyss Sequence 8's ST +2, throws
  wherever the digested character is built. This was read off the code, not
  reproduced. **This is the successor.**
- **An edit that lowers a POSITIVE ceiling onto the CoR total** does not latch
  the loss; the next CoR gain does. This was the design review's finding. It
  does not crash, and it is pre-existing.
- **Selling a secondary refunds points without limit.** With Basic Speed and
  Basic Move at −100 the budget bar read `-808 of 100 points, 908 spare`.
  The floors cap the refund on HP, FP, Will and Per, but not on the two
  rows they do not guard. Whether a reduced secondary counts against
  chapter 3's "-40 points of disadvantages" (book line 1120) is a question
  for the book, and it was not asked here.
- **The builder prints bought values without potion grants.** Before this
  slice it showed HP `0` beside a sheet reading `2 / 2`. Pre-existing.

## 6ej. The button that printed nothing about its own roll

6ei ended on one thing seen and not touched: *"the block that carries the
Drink button prints nothing about the roll it is about to make — the target
and the early-advancement cost are printed on the PREVIOUS block."* 6ei also
recorded that three sentences of that kind about this screen had gone into
the record unread, so this one was checked before it was believed.

**It is true, and the design review quoted both conditions.** *Drink and roll*
is drawn in the branch `drunk.canDrink(chosen)`, and `canDrink` admits only
the NEXT Sequence. The target and the cost were printed by `DigestionTracker`
alone, drawn under `if (isCurrentPotion && !session.isLost)` — the CURRENT
Sequence. One block cannot be both. So the one irreversible roll on the
pathway screen — 3d6 ≤ 1 at 0% digestion — was made beside neither number,
in an app where every other roll prints its target before it rolls.

### What shipped

- `PotionConsumption.corCostFor(state)` — the floor before full digestion,
  nothing at 100%. `attempt` charges it. That decision was written twice
  before: once in `attempt`, and once as a choice of string in the tracker.
- `Corruption.isLostAfter(cor, delta, max)` — whether a gain ends the
  character. `BeyonderSession.gainCor` asks it, and so does the screen.
- `pcrLine(state)` — `3d6 ≤ T`, and ` — on success +N CoR minimum; the GM may
  charge more` when there is a cost. The tracker prints `next potion rolls` in
  front of it; the Drink block prints `at D% digested, rolls` in front of it.
- `drinkLine(state, cor, ceilingAfter)` — that line, and when the charge
  reaches the ceiling of the potion being drunk INTO: *"Maximum CoR after this
  potion is M; C CoR reaches it — lost to corruption even if the potion
  integrates."*

`drink` and `stillShows` are unchanged, and no number from the screen goes to
the session. A mortal's *Drink this potion* prints no line: it makes no roll.

### The half the design review added

My sketch printed the target and the cost and left the landing ceiling out,
and asked whether that made the line misleading. **MEDIUM: it does.** A line
with a target and a cost reads as a complete account of the risk, and the
book's own arithmetic makes the commonest early advancement unsurvivable: a
floor of 10 CoR against a Will of 10. The session has reported that since M4
— `PcrDialog` titles it *"The potion integrates — and takes them"* — but only
AFTER the tap. And the zero-cost case is the Will-lowering potion that M4
paid for once already: nothing charged, and the ceiling lands on the total.
Both are one predicate, so the warning is `isLostAfter` with whatever the
cost is. Its LOW was the wording: "advancing now also costs 10+ CoR" left it
implicit that the charge is on success only and that the app charges the
floor.

### Two things this settles about 6eh and 6ei

**6eh's "the potion roll is left, and its window is open" is closed, and
6ei closed it without saying so.** 6ei corrected the REASON that paragraph
gave (the stepper and Drink do not share a screen) and left the verdict
standing. The input list, checked by the review rather than written by it:
the printed target is `targetFor(drunk.digestion)`; the rolled one is
`targetFor(session.state.digestion)` at the tap; and `stillShows` lets the
tap through only when `state == drunk`, on a data class whose equality
includes `digestion`. The cost reads the same field. What is outside that
equality is the dice and `maxCorFor(next)`, and neither is an input to the
target. So the potion roll is the ninth of 6eg's nine pairs, closed from the
other side: the screen does not hand over the number it printed, the session
declines to act unless it would compose the same one.

**`onSamePotion` has a reviewer now.** 6ei shipped it with two mutations and
a grep. The review's answers: no sequence of taps inside one frame applies a
CoR step against a ceiling that is no longer the session's; the KDoc's claim
that a digestion step cannot move the ceiling is true (`maxCorFor` →
`PotionDigestion.of` → `Corruption.maxFor`, none reading `digestion`); and one
legal tap IS dropped — a CoR step after a successful Drink, before the
redraw, even when the ceiling did not move — which is the design, and has a
test. The review could not see the handler under the rewritten comment at
`MainActivity.kt:1564` because my file range stopped short of it; it is
`if (outcome != null) return@TextButton` and then `SelfControl.rollAgainst
(check, target, appDice)`, read here, which is what the comment says.

### Tests and mutations

RED first: unresolved references in all three test files. Then eight tests —
two in `core:rules`, six in the new `PathwayScreenTest` — and six single
mutations, each restored from a copy:

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| the cost charged at 100% too | *what advancing costs can be asked before the roll is made* |
| `isLostAfter` ignores the gain | *a gain that reaches the maximum ends the character* |
| `gainCor` latches on the old total | *reaching the maximum latches the loss*, and two more |
| `drinkLine` warns on the total before the cost | *an advancement whose cost reaches the ceiling…* |
| `pcrLine` drops the cost clause | *the roll is printed with what advancing early costs* |
| the warning names `$cor`, not `${cor + cost}` | the same test, after the diff review |

The sixth is the diff review's: it survived my first five assertions, which
only ever started from 0 CoR, where the two totals differ by exactly the
cost and the sentence was matched on its other words.

**What no test catches, and is refused one.** The call site: `drinkLine
(drunk, printedCor, maxCorFor(chosen))`. Passing `maxCor` — the ceiling of
the potion being digested — survives the suite, and so does removing the
`Text`. The review asked for a Compose test. Section 6 already answers that:
composables are device-only until there is a reason better than coverage.
The device pass below was chosen to tell those two ceilings apart.

### On the SM-T570

Antiquarian Dealer, a mortal with Will 10, down the Abyss pathway — because
Sequence 9 lowers Will and Sequence 8 lowers it again, so the two ceilings
differ on one screen.

| State | Screen |
|---|---|
| mortal, Sequence 9 block | `Drink this potion`, no line |
| Sequence 9 at 0%, its own block | `next potion rolls 3d6 ≤ 1 — on success +10 CoR minimum; the GM may charge more` |
| the same, Sequence 8 block | `Drink and roll`, then `at 0% digested, rolls 3d6 ≤ 1 — on success +10 CoR minimum; the GM may charge more. Maximum CoR after this potion is 8; 10 CoR reaches it — lost to corruption even if the potion integrates` |
| the tracker beside it | `0 / 9` |
| Sequence 9 at 100%, Sequence 8 block | `at 100% digested, rolls 3d6 ≤ 19` and no warning |

`8` beside `0 / 9` is `maxCorFor(chosen)` and not `maxCor`. The line wraps to
four rows under the button and sat on the divider; it has 8 dp below it now,
re-read on the rebuilt app. Not exercised: a tap on *Drink and roll*.

The tablet was showing another app, in landscape, when this began. The first
dump after launch was portrait; the next three had coordinates past 1200,
which only a landscape display can produce; then a dump failed with *"null
root node"*, the helper served the previous file, focus read
`NotificationShade`, and a screencap showed the app in portrait, back on the
character list. Rotation was locked at 0 throughout. The cause was not
established — only that the display turned twice and the navigation state did
not survive it. **Print the focus and the rotation beside every dump on a
shared device**; every dump after that one did.

The premade this left changed on the tablet: Antiquarian Dealer is a
Sequence 9 Criminal at 100% digestion and 0 CoR.

### The line that could crash its own block

Found by the last review, after `b94a5fe`, and fixed in the commit after it,
before either was pushed. `drinkLine` asks `Corruption.isLostAfter`, which
goes through `requireWillScore` and THROWS for a ceiling below 1 — pinned by
*a maximum below one is a bad call, not a lost character*. Before this slice
`maxCorFor(chosen)` was evaluated only on the tap. Now it is evaluated while
the next block is DRAWN, so such a character would have crashed the pathway
screen by being browsed.

**It is reachable.** `will` is a priced row in `secondary_costs.json`, and
the builder's `−` is enabled down to `-MAX_SECONDARY_DELTA_MAGNITUDE`, a
hundred steps — an overflow bound, not a rule. RED with the
`IllegalArgumentException` itself; then `drinkLine` prints the state —
*"Will after this potion is 0, which is no CoR ceiling"* — and asks nothing.
Not a `maxOf`: that would print a ceiling the character does not have. Not
run on a device: it needs a premade's Will bought down ten steps.

Tests: 1761 Kotlin (1244 `core:rules`, 497 `app`, 20 `core:model`), the
three modules counted after `--rerun-tasks`, and 357 Python.

**The successor is what that exposed.** Every other caller that takes a
ceiling to `Corruption` is a TAP, and each still throws for that character:
the CoR steppers, a successful Drink, a ritual's CoR (`MainActivity.kt:1155`
and `:1195`) and Soul Debt in `spend`. Whether a Will below 1 is a character
the book allows is a question for the book, and the builder's bound is where
it is answered or refused — not a coercion at each of those sites.

One more thing seen on the way and not touched: the
warning is plain `bodySmall`, the same weight as the sentence it ends, where
`CorruptionTracker` turns its own total to the error colour one point short
of the ceiling.

## 6ei. Two taps, one frame, on a device

6eh named a stale check on Drink and gave its reason: the `±5%` digestion
stepper and Drink are on the same screen, so a step and a drink inside one
frame roll a Potion Consumption Roll off the printed target. **That reason
was false, and the slice it named was real for a different one.**

**The stepper and Drink are never on screen together.** `DigestionTracker`
is drawn only where `isCurrentPotion` holds — on the block of the potion
already drunk. Drink is drawn where `drunk.canDrink(chosen)` holds — on the
NEXT block. The design review refuted the claim from `PathwayScreen.kt:280`
and it is two lines to check; I had written it into the slice log and the
handover from the layout in my head. **Third time in three slices that a
sentence of mine about this screen's reachability went into the record
unread**: 6ef's missing reviews, 6eg's census, this.

**What the review found instead: Drink had no re-entrancy guard**, alone
among the roll buttons in this app. `{ pcr = session.drink(chosen, dice,
maxCorFor) }`, where every other one opens with `if (outcome != null)
return`. The first call advances the session, and the second, from the same
composition, hands `drink` the same `chosen` — which its own `require`
refuses by throwing.

### Reproduced

This is the first claim in the 6ef–6ei chain to be produced on a device
rather than read off the code. SM-T570, a build with the guard neutered, a
mortal premade on *Drink this potion*:

| Injector | Result |
|---|---|
| `input tap … & input tap … & wait` | no crash — two JVMs start too far apart |
| one `cat` of eighteen raw events into `/dev/input/event1` | `Permission denied`; the shell is in group `input` and SELinux refuses anyway. Left alone |
| `monkey --throttle 0 -f` a script of two `Tap(475,608,1)` | **`FATAL EXCEPTION: main`** |

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: BeyonderState(pathway=Fool, sequence=9,
  digestion=0) is not the next potion after BeyonderState(pathway=Fool,
  sequence=9, digestion=0)
    at com.pathways.app.BeyonderSession.drink(BeyonderSession.kt:388)
    at com.pathways.app.PathwayScreenKt.PathwayScreen$lambda$…(PathwayScreen.kt:272)
```

The app died to the launcher; the first drink had already been persisted.
The same script against the guarded build: one potion drunk, *"digesting:
0%"*, no crash.

**What that settles and what it does not.** Two taps a few milliseconds apart
reach one composition's handler before the screen redraws — so the premise
6ef, 6eg and 6eh all rested on is true on hardware, and the comment at
`MainActivity.kt:1568` that said *"Compose recomposes on the state write, so
the two taps are two frames"* is false. That comment's REFUSAL was right
(do not recompute inside the handler — which is 6eg's whole direction) and
only its second reason was wrong; it is rewritten to say so. What is not
settled is a finger: monkey's taps are milliseconds apart and a human
double-tap is on the order of a hundred. The crash is real and the guard is
cheap; nobody has shown a person can cause it.

### What shipped (`a33eb0b`)

Two questions on the session, and the handlers ask before acting:

- `stillShows(printed, printedCor)` — `!isLost && state == printed && cor ==
  printedCor`. Drink asks it. A stale tap does nothing; the screen redraws
  and the GM taps again, looking at what is true. `drink` itself, requires
  and all, is unchanged: the session still takes no number from the screen
  as authoritative, it only declines to act on a picture that has moved.
- `onSamePotion(printed)` — pathway and Sequence only. The CoR steppers ask
  it.

**Two predicates because the design review and the diff review pulled one
apart.** The design review's first HIGH was that CoR had to be compared: at
9 of 20, a `+1` and a successful early advancement inside one frame charge
10 and end the character, and CoR IS drawn beside Drink. Its second was the
reverse order — a CoR step from the composition before a Drink applies
against the ceiling that Drink may just have lowered, which is the
Will-lowering-potion defect M4 already paid for once. So the steppers got a
guard too, on the same predicate — and the diff review found that it then
dropped a CoR step taken in the same frame as a digestion step, because
state equality includes digestion. The steppers' question is narrower than
Drink's: only a new potion moves their ceiling. **`onSamePotion` was written
AFTER that review and no reviewer has read it** (6ej: one has, and it is
correct), nor the rewritten comment at
`MainActivity.kt:1568`. What stands behind it is two mutations and one
grep: the claim that a digestion step cannot move the ceiling was checked
against `PotionDigestion.kt` and `Corruption.kt`, neither of which reads
`digestion`, on the screen where a claim of exactly this kind had just been
found false.

`edits` is compared by neither. Nothing on the pathway screen changes it,
and `maxCorFor` reads the live edits when it is called.

### Tests and mutations

Three tests on `BeyonderSession`, RED twice (unresolved reference, then a
stub comparing `state` alone, which fails on the lost character and on the
CoR step). Seven single mutations, each caught:

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| drop `!isLost` | *a lost character's screen shows nothing to act on* |
| drop `state == printed` | *a screen drawn before the session moved…* |
| drop `cor == printedCor` | the same |
| add `printed != null &&` (a mortal can never drink) | *a mortal's screen shows the truth until the first potion* |
| `!isLost` → `!lost` (lost to corruption slips through) | *a lost character's screen…* |
| CoR steps compare the whole state | *a screen drawn before the session moved…* |
| CoR steps ignore the Sequence | the same |

The fourth and fifth are the diff review's, and both had survived its
reading of my first two tests: nothing asserted the null picture a mortal
has, and "lost" was only ever reached by a failed roll.

- Unguarded build, two taps: the crash above. Guarded build, the same two
  taps: one drink, no crash.
- Two taps on Corruption `+1` from one script: `0 / 10` → `2 / 10`. Both

- **And everything 6ef, 6eg and 6eh had only an emulator behind.** The ritual

**No successor is named.** One thing seen on the way and not touched: the

## 6eh. Seven more targets, each composed once

6eg's corrected census named this: seven rolls still printed a target and
then composed it a second time in the click handler, and the Fright Check
wrote its sum in the screen and again in the engine. None could throw. They
are fixed on the owner's rule rather than on a failure — *the same predicate
at two call sites is the defect, not the drift it produces.*

**What shipped (`55bfa83`).** Each engine gains `rollAgainst`, its older entry
point is that roll with the target composed first, and each handler passes
the value on screen.

| Roll | Engine | Handler now calls |
|---|---|---|
| Boon | none new | `RitualResolution.rollAgainst(target, dice)` |
| Concentration | `rollAgainst(target, disturbed, source)` | the same, behind `!disturbed` |
| Self-control | `rollAgainst(check, target, source)` | the same |
| Divination | `rollAgainst(target, source, requiresCritical)` | the same |
| Fright Check | `targetFor(will, modifier)`, `rollAgainst(target, source, effects)` | prints and rolls one `target` |
| Spirit Vision | `rollAgainst(target, source, parts)` | `parts` built once beside `target` |
| Detection | `partsFor(...)`, `rollAgainst(target, source, parts)` | the same |

`Boons.attempt` used to repeat `targetFor`'s adjustments line for line; it
goes through `targetFor` now.

**Detection's caption changed, and that is the half that is not cosmetic.**
It was `attributeLine` plus the SUMMED modifier plus shock and hurt, assembled
in the screen, while the result carried an itemised list built in the engine
— two renderings of one breakdown. It prints `partsFor(...)` now, the list
the result holds, so the line before the roll and the line after it are the
same line.

### The design review, before code

`codex exec`, the eight pairs lettered and the handlers named. Its verdicts
shaped three of the seven:

- **Concentration: SHIP WITH CHANGE.** My sketch passed "only what the outcome
  needs beyond the target", which dropped `disturbed` — the guard that says
  the book calls for no roll at all. Kept only on `attempt`, it would have
  left the path production takes unguarded. It is a parameter of
  `rollAgainst`, and the handler reads it at click time on purpose: it is
  eligibility, not a term of the target.
- **Spirit Vision and Detection: SHIP WITH CHANGE.** Passing the target alone
  leaves the breakdown composed at two sites, *"making the change cosmetic"*.
  Both pass the parts they printed.
- **Rolling the printed target is wrong nowhere among the seven.** Nothing a
  handler mutates before rolling is a term of its target; Spirit Vision spends
  SPI first, and SPI is not in its number.
- **The wrappers stay.** `attempt(inputs)` loses its production caller in all
  eight engines and survives as the composed convenience the tests use.
  Deleting them and rewriting ~60 call sites as `rollAgainst(targetFor(...))`
  was judged the larger and less safe change.

**One verdict not taken: the potion roll, and its window is still open.**
The review said SHIP WITH CHANGE — *"share a session-owned prepared target
tied to its state, updating it when state changes."* A stored target is a
cache of a pure function of one field and has to be invalidated, so that
shape is refused. **But this section's first reason for leaving the pair
alone was not a reason.** It said the screen and the session read the same
state and the predicate is written once, in the engine — which was equally
true of Divination before this slice, whose preview and whose `attempt` both
went through `Divination.targetFor`. One predicate, two call sites, one state
read at two moments: the same shape, fixed there and left here.

What actually differs is the layer. Everywhere else the dialog owns the
inputs, so handing the engine the number it printed is handing it the truth.
Here `BeyonderSession` owns state that is PERSISTED, and it must not take a
number from the screen as authoritative — that is the one caller that has to
re-read. **CORRECTION (6ei): the window this paragraph went on to describe
does not exist.** It said the `±5%` digestion stepper is on the same screen
as Drink. It is not — the tracker is drawn on the current potion's block and
Drink on the next one — and the claim was never checked against
`PathwayScreen.kt:280`. The stale check it named was worth building for a
different reason, which 6ei found and reproduced: Drink had no re-entrancy
guard, and CoR, which IS drawn beside it, prices the advancement. **(6ej):
and that guard closes the window itself — `stillShows` compares digestion.**

### The mutations, and what "survives" turned out to mean

**The first pass was mine: eight single edits, one survived.** `Boons.attempt`
ignoring `chosen` and `gmValue` left every test green. No test had ever
passed a modifier through `attempt` — only through `targetFor` — so the
function's forwarding was pinned by nothing, before this slice and after it.

**The diff review then proposed seven more, assessed by reading.** Run against
the whole suite instead:

| Review's mutation | Result | Path |
|---|---|---|
| Concentration rolls, then refuses | **survived** | production |
| `SelfControl.attempt` passes Will for IQ | **survived** | wrapper |
| Divination grades a demoted roll as a success | caught, `AntiDivinationTest` | — |
| `FrightCheck.against` drops its `effects` table | **survived** | wrapper |
| Spirit Vision reads every roll by outcome | **survived** | production |
| Detection reads the row at margin 0 | caught, `the deeper success band wins` | — |
| `Boons.attempt` drops `cor` | **survived** | wrapper |

Five of seven, which is a reviewer reading correctly without running
anything. Four are taken and each is RED-proved; the `effects` one is
refused, because that parameter is a test seam no test passes, so pinning it
pins nothing a caller reads.

**Two things in that table are worth more than the fixes.**

- **No test had ever rolled a Spirit Vision SUCCESS through the engine.** The
  one `attempt` call in `SpiritVisionTest` fails its roll. Reading a success
  by outcome instead of by margin returned the bare "Success" row for every
  margin and nothing noticed. That is the production path, and the row is
  what the dialog prints.
- **Three of the five are forwarding bugs in functions production no longer
  calls.** This slice is what made `attempt` test-only, and a wrapper that
  forwards wrongly now misleads only the suite — which is worse than it
  sounds, because the suite is what reads it. Each wrapper's forwarding is
  pinned by an assertion chosen so the dropped argument changes the number:
  Impulsive is keyed on IQ-2 with Will 7 and IQ 12, the prayer carries 3 CoR,
  the boon carries a modifier AND a pick inside it.

**And one "survived" was not a survival.** A script that edited two test files
failed half-way on an import that file does not have, so two mutations ran
against tests that had not changed and passed. `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` under a
mutation means the guard did not fire; it does not say the guard exists.

## 6eg. One target, printed and then rolled

6ef closed one stale-state window in `RitualDialog`'s Roll handler and
recorded two more beside it as "the nearest thing to a named successor". This
slice closes all three, and does it by reversing the direction 6ef took.

**Reading state later cannot fix it.** `ce463ab` made the handler read the
pick "NOW". But a click handler belongs to the composition that drew it: a
Roll lambda from composition N holds the state objects N's keyed `remember`s
created. After a tap on a mode chip, `mode` (unkeyed) reads the new value and
`preparation`, `link` and `flourish` (`remember(mode)`) read N's old objects.
No amount of reading at click time makes every input current, because the old
lambda never sees the new objects. The only pairing that is consistent by
construction is the other one: everything composition N computed.

**And the handler was the second of two call sites.** The dialog composed its
target while drawing — `targetFor(...)`, fifteen arguments, for the printed
`3d6 ≤ N` — and then handed `attempt(...)` the same fifteen in the handler.
6ef's device pass said so in its own words: *"nothing but those two `vs`
lines pins them to each other."* That is the warrant for this slice. The race
would not have carried it alone.

**What shipped (`873813c`).** `RitualResolution.rollAgainst(target, source)`
is what `attempt` did after composing its target; `attempt` is now
`rollAgainst(targetFor(...), ...)`, so there is one `classify` path and
`Boons.attempt` is untouched. The handler is one line,
`RitualResolution.rollAgainst(target, dice)`, where `target` is the
composition's own `val` — non-null in that branch, and the value on screen.
The handler now reads exactly one state, the `outcome` re-entrancy guard;
`spiOwed` and `hpOwed` were composition values already.

`pickInside` and the row-held picks stay. They are what bring a pick back
when the GM returns to its row, and they filter during composition; the
click-time reads 6ef added are gone, and the comments that gave the handler
as their reason are rewritten rather than left to expire.

`rollAgainst` takes a bare `Int` and does not ask where it came from. That is
deliberate and is in its KDoc: `classify` needs the dice and the number to
agree, and `pushed` has always re-read a roll against a target no `targetFor`
returned.

### The census this rests on

`grep -n "\.targetFor(\|\.attempt(\|\.against(\|\.rollAgainst(\|SkillRoll\.at(" app/src/main/kotlin/com/pathways/app/*.kt`
returns 27 lines. One is not a roll (`AntiDivination.against` composes a
penalty). The rest, each read at both ends:

**A printed target and a roll composed at two call sites — eight, one fixed:**

| Roll | Preview | Roll handler passes | Can it throw? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ritual | `targetFor`, 15 args | 8 state reads beside 4 composition values | yes — **fixed here** |
| Divination | `targetFor(skill, difficulty, extras)` | `difficulty` (state) beside `extras` (value) | no, a sum |
| Self-control | `targetFor`, at TWO sites (the trait list's base figure, the dialog's) | `modifier` (state) beside `fromState` (value) | no, a sum |
| Boon | `Boons.targetFor` | composition values and parameters | no |
| Detection | `Detection.targetFor` | composition values and parameters | no |
| Concentration | `Concentration.targetFor` | parameters and `fromTraits.total` | no |
| Spirit Vision | `SpiritVision.targetFor` | parameters | no |
| Potion Consumption | `PathwayScreen` prints `targetFor(digestion)` | `BeyonderSession` calls `attempt(state)` | no — two FILES |

**A sum written in the screen and again in the engine — one.** The Fright
Check prints `3d6 vs ${will + effective}` and then calls
`FrightCheck.against(will, effective, …)`, which adds the same two numbers.

**One call site, nothing printed before the dice — three.** The skill roll,
the attack and the Acrobatic Dodge compose their modifiers inside the handler
from unkeyed state and print the target only off the outcome.

**Already rolling against a number they were handed — four.** Both
`DamageDialog` rolls, the vital rolls and the fright recovery call
`SuccessRoll.against(target, dice)`.

**This table's first version listed seven pairs and called the remaining six
"available, not owed". Both were wrong.** Its header query returns the potion
pair and the Fright Check and the table listed neither; the skill roll, the
most-used roll in the app, was not in it at all. And "a mismatch nobody has
seen" is a drift argument, which the owner's rule rejects in so many words:
*the same predicate at two call sites is the defect, not the drift it
produces.* This section's own warrant — one target instead of two — applies
to every row it had left. None of the seven can throw, which is why they are
not this slice; they are the next one.

**A comment in the tree disagrees with this slice's premise, and neither is
proven.** `MainActivity.kt:1566`, above the self-control roll: *"Compose
recomposes on the state write, so the two taps are two frames."* Codex's
reading in 6ef is that two taps can land inside one frame. Neither has been
reproduced on a device. This slice does not depend on which is right — one
target instead of two is the reason it shipped — and the comment is left
alone for that reason.

### The reviews

**Design, before any code** (`codex exec`, three questions, the Roll handler
named). No finding on the handler, the entity answer, or the engine shape.
Two things worth keeping:

- *Ask then Roll in one frame* is not reachable in HEAD or after: the Ask
  button exists only while `answer == null`, and that same condition
  withholds Roll.
- **One behaviour does change, and it is the contract rather than a defect.**
  A language the caster cannot speak, tapped in the same frame as Roll, used
  to reach the engine's refusal and throw. It now rolls the target that was
  on screen when Roll was pressed.

**Diff, before the commit.** No finding on behaviour preservation (same
defaults, same order of draws, same arguments to `classify`), none on the
handler, and **one LOW, taken**: the new test's misfire used
`scripted(5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4)`, and `scripted` repeats its last face, so a draw
taken and thrown away between the ritual's roll and the table's reads 4+4+4
either way. The faces are 4, 4, 3 now. RED-proved by adding that discarded
`source.roll(6)`: the test fails on `criticalRoll`, 8 for 9.

Two things the review did not say and the fix made visible:

- `assertEquals(attempt(...), rollAgainst(targetFor(...)))` cannot see a
  change in draw order any more, because `attempt` IS `rollAgainst` — both
  sides move together. What pins the order is the two literal numbers beside
  it. The equality still earns its place: it is what fails if `attempt`
  composes a target and then rolls against something else.
- The older `a severe misfire rolls the critical table at minus two` uses
  4, 4, 4 as well and has the same blind side. Left as it is: the mutation it
  would miss is now caught one test down, and that is one check on one fact.

RED for the function itself was taken twice, as in 6ef: unresolved reference,
then a stub that judged the dice against `target - 1` while reporting
`target`, which fails `rolled.roll.target` 15 for 16 — and fails 6ef's own
pick test with it.

### On a device

Emulator again (`Medium_Tablet`, API 35), same carrier. The one claim to
