- Full, Good at +2: `3d6 ≤ 15`, then **`3d6: 8 vs 15`**.
- Quick, Strong at +3: `3d6 ≤ 16`, `preparation +0, +3 strong link`, then
  **`3d6: 9 vs 16`**.

No `com.pathways` line in `AndroidRuntime:E`. The one-frame race was not
reproduced before the fix and cannot be exercised after it.

Tests: 1743 Kotlin (1235 `core:rules`, 488 `app`, 20 `core:model`) after
`--rerun-tasks`; the 356 Python tests were not re-run, nothing under `tools/`
having changed.

**The successor is the seven rows of the first table that still say "no",
and the Fright Check's inline sum.** It overturns the verdict this section
first recorded, so its decomposition is reviewed before code, with the
handlers named. Two things to settle there rather than assume: whether each
engine needs a new entry point at all (the Boon dialog can call
`RitualResolution.rollAgainst` as it stands), and whether the potion pair is
the same defect or a screen reading the state its session owns.

## 6ef. The span a chip printed and the roll never took

6ee named this slice with its evidence: chapter 7's three ritual tables print
cells that are a span or a floor, and `RitualDialog` showed the span on the
chip and applied the end nearer zero, with no way to reach the rest. The
cells, as `ModifierRangeTest` now pins them by name:

| Table | Cell | Offered |
|---|---|---|
| Full preparation | `Good +1 to +2` | +1, +2 |
| Full preparation | `Poor -1 to -2` | -1, -2 |
| Full preparation | `None -4 or worse` | -4, -5, -6, -7 |
| Quick preparation | `Poor / None -2 to -4` | -2, -3, -4 |
| Target link | `Strong +2 to +3` | +2, +3 |
| Target link | `Weak +0 to -1` | +0, -1 |

**The warrant had already died.** `RitualResolution.targetFor`'s KDoc called
the near end *"the gentle reading the darkness row and the fright triggers
already settled"*. 6dz gave the darkness row a picker and the fright trigger
has had a stepper since M4, so the sentence named two precedents and neither
held. And the book's own worked rituals use the far ends: rituals 3 and 7
print *"Long-used sanctified space +2"* (Good's far end) and ritual 4 prints
*"True name known +3"* (Strong's). `GoldenRitualTest` had accepted those by
comparing against `modifier || best` by hand — values no caller could produce.

**What shipped (`80fe956`).** `RitualMode.valueFor(row, chosen)` holds a pick
to its OWN cell, on the contract `CommonModifiers.valueFor` already set: a
span takes anything between its ends, a floor anything at or past it on the
far side of zero, and a cell printing one figure takes that figure only. +3 is
Excellent's and is refused for Good. The pick is threaded by name through
`modifierTotal`, `targetFor` and `attempt`. **Unpicked is still the near end,
and that is this app's default, not the book's rule** — the book says only
that *"the GM determines the Preparation Modifier from the player's
declarations"* (p. 63). `-4 or worse` offers three steps past its figure
(`OPEN_END_STEPS`, the constant `spiChoices` already used as a bare 3); the
engine takes -9 as readily, so the limit is the screen's.

`GoldenRitualTest` now asks the ENGINE whether a printed value lands on a
cell, and asserts the value RETURNED — an engine that validated a pick and
then applied the near end would accept all of them and produce none.

**Both gates ran before the commit, and this section first said neither
had.** Its first draft read *"No record of a decomposition review exists"*,
checked against the commit body and this log. The third place is
`~/.codex/sessions`, which holds both, forty and seventeen minutes before
`80fe956`:

- **Design review, 00:28, SHIP on all three questions.** The API shape (two
  nullable picks passed by name), stale state, and the book — which is where
  *"near-end defaults are app policy, not a book rule"* comes from, with line
  4119 quoted.
- **Diff review, 00:39: no finding on the dialog, two MEDIUMs and a LOW in
  the tests, all three taken** and visible in the commit — the interior `-3`
  that a first-and-last check cannot see, `picked.roll.target` beside
  `picked.target`, and the golden tests comparing the value RETURNED rather
  than the absence of a refusal.

**An absence claim names the corpus it was checked against (6da)**, and this
one named two places out of three.

### The mutation pass, executed

Six single edits, each `cp`-restored, each read by the test it reddened and
not by exit code (the first attempt at a baseline failed on Gradle's `Unable
to delete directory` and looked exactly like a caught mutation):

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `minOf..maxOf` → `near..far` | `RitualModeTest` ×2, `GoldenRitualTest` (links) |
| open-ended side check flipped | `RitualModeTest` *or worse runs away from zero* |
| single-figure branch → `require(true)` | `RitualModeTest` *a cell that prints one number* |
| `targetFor` drops the picks | `RitualResolutionTest` *a pick reaches the target and the roll* |
| `attempt` drops the picks | the same test |
| `pickedWithin` validates, returns `near` | seven tests across all four files |

The first one says more than its row: `-2 to -4` runs downward too, so the
empty-range bug `Weak +0 to -1` was written to guard would have refused every
pick in a second cell.

### A third review, after the commit (Codex, `codex exec`, three questions)

**MEDIUM, taken (`ce463ab`).** The picks were `remember(mode, preparation)`
and `remember(mode, link)`, under a comment calling the row key
"load-bearing" because `targetFor` throws on a pick outside its cell. **A
keyed `remember` resets at the next recomposition, and a click handler reads
state as it stands now.** Good's +2, a tap on Excellent and a tap on Roll
inside one frame hand `attempt` Excellent with a 2 it refuses, and the throw
is in the handler. The pick is now held WITH its row
(`Pair<RitualPreparation, Int>`) and read through `pickInside(row, held)`,
which answers null for any other row — filtered on read rather than cleared
on change, which is 6dz's own design for `overrides` and was sitting in the
sibling dialogs the whole time. The Roll handler calls `pickInside` itself
instead of using the value the composition drew with.

**Two reviews had been asked about exactly this and cleared it, and both
were right about what they were asked.** The design review's question was
whether pick and row can *"disagree for one composition"*, and its answer —
*"there is no composition with the new row and old pick"* — is true. The
window is BETWEEN compositions, in a handler, and the third review found it
because its question named the Roll button's `attempt()` instead. The design
review had even written the fix down as its strongest objection to the shape
it approved: *"nullable integers separate a choice from its owning row … a
wrapper could preserve that association."* **A reviewer answers the question's
frame; ask about the handlers by name.**

RED was taken twice on purpose: the unresolved reference first, then a
pass-through `held?.second`, which fails with the engine's own
`IllegalArgumentException` on the line that hands Excellent a 2. **A missing
function proves nothing about a behaviour (6ec).**

One behaviour changed with it and is stated in `docs/HOW-TO-PLAY.md`: a pick
now comes back when the GM returns to its row, shown selected. Under the
keyed `remember` it was forgotten.

**The finding indicts its model, and the model is NOT repaired (6ds).**
The query is `grep -rn "by remember([a-zA-Z]" app/src/main/kotlin`: 43 hits,
most of them dialog-open flags and stored outcomes. A keyed state that is
validated only DURING composition is sound, which is what `DivinationDialog`
(`spiFor`, line 203), `ArtifactDialog` (`costOf`, line 61) and
`DetectionDialog` do. `RitualDialog`'s Roll handler is the one traced that
hands delegate reads to a validating call:

- `preparation`, `link` and `flourish` are `remember(mode)` and are passed
  beside a fresh `mode`; `modifierTotal` refuses the old mode's row, link or
  flourish under the new one.
- `declaration` is a composition-time value built from `spiChoice`,
  `hpSacrificed` and `sentientBeings`, passed beside a fresh `complexity`;
  `PowerSources.modifierTotal` validates the pair.

`Divination.attempt`'s handler (line 663) was not traced further.

**Neither window was reproduced, and the one fixed is no more reachable than
the ones left.** Each needs two taps between two frames, which is two
fingers, and in Full mode on the tested tablet the preparation chips and Roll
are about 1750 px apart in a dialog showing about 1200 — never on screen
together. The pick was fixed and the rest was not for a reason of cost, not
of risk: its fix is one function and is the design the sibling dialogs
already use, while the others mean re-shaping six pieces of state this slice
did not touch. Recorded as the nearest thing to a named successor.

**LOW, refused** — and not the pre-commit LOW on the same test, which was
about the value returned and was taken. *"Worked rituals 3/4/7 reach `valueFor` only, never
`targetFor`/`attempt`."* True, and the reviewer's own next clause is the
reason: `RitualResolutionTest` pins the forwarding, and mutations four and
five above RED-prove it. The golden test's question is whether a printed
value lands on a cell. One check on one fact (6dv); a second forwarding
assertion built from worked examples would also have to route around the
discrepancies those examples already record.

Q3, whether the chips offered and the picks accepted can disagree: no
finding, and `ModifierRangeTest` walks every offered value of every such row
through the engine.

### On a device

Emulator, `Medium_Tablet`, API 35, 2560×1600 — not the SM-T570 the earlier
slices used; no hardware was attached. The carrier is the Academic Researcher
after one Fool Sequence 9 potion (no published sheet has Ritualistic Magic),
skill 13.

- **Full.** `Adequate +0` draws no pick row. `Good +1 to +2` draws *"The book
  prints +1 to +2 — the GM picks:"* with +1 selected before anything is
  tapped. Tapping +2 takes the target `3d6 ≤ 13` → `3d6 ≤ 15`, breakdown
  `preparation +2`. **Roll printed `3d6: 15 vs 15` — "The ritual holds"**,
  which the unpicked +1 would have missed by one.
- **Row switches.** Good +2 → Excellent: no pick row, no crash. → `None -4 or
  worse`: -4, -5, -6, -7 with -4 selected. → Good: +2 selected again.
- **Quick.** `Poor / None -2 to -4` offers -2, -3, -4. With -3 and `Strong
  +2 to +3` at +3: `3d6 ≤ 13`, breakdown `preparation -3, +3 strong link`,
  and Roll printed `3d6: 15 vs 13`. Strong switched off with its +3 held: no
  crash. `Weak +0 to -1` offers +0 then -1, in that order. Strong again: +3.

The preview and the roll are two call sites handed the picks separately, and
nothing but those two `vs` lines pins them to each other. The one-frame race
itself was not reproduced; `pickInside`'s test is what covers it.

Dump coordinates were true pixels on the emulator, sheet and dialog both, so
6du's per-window scale is a fact about that tablet and not about
`uiautomator`. And a `selected` attribute sits on the chip node while the
text sits on its child, so a dump filtered on text reads every chip as
unselected.

**No successor is named beyond the two handler windows above.** The six cells
were the last spans 6ee found applied with no picker.

## 6ee. The compiler's zero, and the two things beside it

6dl found a vacuous test for free — Kotlin had been printing `Condition is
always 'true'` on every build — and wrote *"read the build's own warnings
before asking for findings"*. Nobody then ran that as a sweep. This is it:
every diagnostic the toolchain will give for nothing, over both languages.

**It is clean, and each zero is recorded with what it can and cannot see.**

| Instrument | Corpus | Hits | Real |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kotlin compiler `w:` lines | 6 source sets, build dirs wiped | 0 | 0 |
| Kotlin parameter never read in its body | 1160 parameters, `src/main` | 2 | 0 |
| Kotlin local never read again | 1736 `val`/`var` matches | 19 | 0 |
| Python compile, `SyntaxWarning` as error | 46 files in `tools/` | 0 | 0 |
| pytest's own warnings | 356 tests | 0 | 0 |
| Python name bound and never loaded (`ast`) | 46 files | 4 | 0 |
| Case-folded haystack, cased needle | 5 Python + 2 Kotlin sites | 0 | 0 |
| Non-ASCII needle against `json.dumps` | 6 sites | 0 | 0 |

**The compiler's zero had to be earned twice.** The first clean run had
`:core:model:compileKotlin FROM-CACHE`, and a cached compile prints nothing —
a zero from a task that did not run. Then the control: one planted line in
`core:model` main and one in its tests, compiled with `--no-build-cache`.
`x is Int` on an `Int` and `x != null && x != null` are both reported.
**`val unused = 1` is not.** So this compiler's silence covers the
always-true class 6dl met and says nothing about a value computed and
dropped, which is the class that would matter here: an input a rule accepts
and ignores.

That blind spot is what the two scanners are for, and both are crude on
purpose. The parameter scan's two hits are `RandomSource.roll(sides)`, an
interface declaration, and `ParryBlock.canParryRanged(style)`, which returns
`false` for every style and whose KDoc says why it takes one anyway. The
local scan's nineteen are seventeen properties at function-body indentation
and two locals read as `(lower..upper)` and `(lo..hi)` — the scanner's own
lookbehind refuses a name preceded by a dot. **A hit list that is all false
positives is the query returning non-zero on real text, which is the control
a clean sweep needs** (6ec).

**Nothing the instruments flagged was a defect. Two things beside their hits
were.**

*The first sat four lines above a dead binding.* `ast` flagged `ch3` in
`test_coverage_intersects_claims_with_mechanical_lines` — bound, never read,
harmless. The test above it, `test_coverage_reports_every_chapter`, ended:

```python
# With no content extracted yet, every chapter is 0% claimed.
assert "0.0%" in report
```

The comment has been false since M1. The assertion outlived it because
**`"100.0%"` contains `"0.0%"`**: it passes on any report with a chapter at a
round ten. Second instance in two slices of a substring that cannot
discriminate (6ed's was `"\nCritical\n"` against a file whose lines open with
a number), and like that one it encoded a fact about a file's FORMAT that was
written down nowhere. It now asserts what its name says — all 22 chapters of
`chapters.json` have a row — and cutting the 7.5 row from the report returns
`['7.5']` where the old line still said `True`.

*The second was the false positive itself.* `val hi = maxOf(printed,
row.otherEnd!!)` in `RollDialog` is read, so the scanner was wrong — and the
line is a **fourth copy of `endsBetween`**. `ModifierRange.kt` exists because
6dz found three dialogs offering a printed span three ways, and its KDoc says
*"Three of this book's modifier tables print a span… one function means a
fourth screen cannot get it wrong a fourth way."* The fourth table is Appendix
A's `Improvised / poor tools -2 to -4`, the fourth screen is the plain skill
roll, and it had its own spelling the whole time:

```kotlin
(lo..hi).sortedBy { kotlin.math.abs(it - printed) }
```

**Not wrong — the same list.** `printed` is always one end of `lo..hi`, so
sorting by distance from it IS the outward walk; checked on both rows that
carry an `otherEnd` (`[1, 2]` and `[-2, -3, -4]`). It is one call now. No
test ships: the two expressions agree on every span a
modifier table can print, so there is no behaviour to pin, and the function the branch now calls already
has `ModifierRangeTest`. What 6dz's sweep could not see is why it survived —
that sweep looked for a `gmValue` parameter nobody passed, and this screen
passed one. **A count in a KDoc is a claim about every other file** (6ci's
lesson about this handover, applied to source).

**The negative-assertion census is recorded as run.** 63 `not in` assertions
in `test_tools.py`; most assert a KEY is absent from a parsed row, which an
extractor can make false. The ones that search text were checked for the two
ways a needle becomes unmatchable by format rather than by fact — a cased
needle against a lowered haystack, a non-ASCII needle against `json.dumps` —
and neither occurs. That is a narrower claim than "no vacuous negative
assertion": it rules out two mechanisms, not the class.

**Gradle's Windows lock cost six builds this session and wore a third
costume**: `Failed to load cache entry … Could not load from local cache:
Unable to delete directory`, on a task that was restoring, not compiling. The
`rm -rf` of the one named directory is not enough when the next attempt
names a sibling; deleting the module's whole `build/` is. And a build
launched as `./gradlew …; echo rc=$?` behind a redirect reports the echo's
status — **the harness said `exited with code 0` over a log reading `BUILD
FAILED`.** Grep the log for `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; do not read the exit code.

**The diff review (Codex, two questions) returned one LOW and it is a
correction to a sentence, not to the code.** I had written that the two
expressions agree "on every input". They do not: at `(0, Int.MIN_VALUE)`
`abs` overflows to a negative key and the old sort would have put the far end
first. That span has two billion members and no table prints one, so the
claim above is narrowed to what is true and the helper stays. It also read
the test for the two ways a row check goes soft — an id `7` matching inside
`7.5`, a title that prefixes a longer title — and the cell delimiters stop
both; and its grep found no other inline bounded span in `app/src/main`.

Both suites re-counted from a wiped tree: 1732 Kotlin (20 / 1227 / 485) and
356 Python. **Not device-verified**, and nothing here needs it: the one
production line changed returns the list it returned before.

**Then I corrected "three" to "four", and that was the same mistake one
size up.** I had counted CALLERS of `endsBetween` and written the number
down as a count of the book's tables. The failure that KDoc exists to prevent
— a printed span the screen collapses to one value — leaves no inline copy
to find, so neither my grep nor the reviewer's could see a fifth. The query
that can is over the data, in two passes:

```python
# every book line printing a signed span, grouped by the file claiming it
re.compile(r'[+\-\u2212\u2013]\d+\s+to\s+[+\-\u2212\u2013]?\d+')
# every content entry storing a second bound
k in ('otherEnd', 'best', 'worstCase')
```

**Eight content files store a second bound, not four**:

| File | Rows | How the screen reaches the span |
|---|---|---|
| `divination_modifiers.json` | 4 | `endsBetween` chips (6dz) |
| `boon_modifiers.json` | 4 | `endsBetween` chips |
| `ranged_modifiers.json` | 1 | `endsBetween` chips (6dz) |
| `common_modifiers.json` | 2 | `endsBetween` chips (this slice) |
| `fright_triggers.json` | 1 | a free ±1 stepper; `FrightCheck.against` takes the number |
| `ritual_preparation.json` | 2 | **nothing** |
| `ritual_quick_preparation.json` | 1 | **nothing** |
| `ritual_target_link.json` | 2 | **nothing** |

The first pass also returns `disadvantages.json` (14 cost ranges, the
instanced-trait feature of 6cb), `spi_affinity.json`, two lines of pathway
prose and three unclaimed lines that 6dy's census already settles (4161,
4289, 4659) — none of them a modifier table.

**The next slice is those five ritual rows, and it is named with its
evidence.** `RitualDialog`'s chips read `Good +1 to +2`, `Poor -1 to -2`,
`Poor / None -2 to -4`, `Strong +2 to +3` and `Weak +0 to -1`, and each
applies `.modifier`, the end nearer zero. `RitualMode.modifierTotal` takes no
override at all, which is why 6dz's sweep — a `gmValue` parameter no caller
passes — could not see it: **there is no parameter to leave defaulted.**
Three things make it a defect rather than a reading:

- **Its recorded warrant is dead on both legs.** 6q applied the near end as
  *"the same gentle reading as the darkness row"*, and
  `RitualResolution.targetFor`'s KDoc still cites *"the gentle reading the
  darkness row and the fright triggers already settled"*. 6k's own words for
  darkness were *"applies the gentle end **for now**"*, 6dz ended that, and
  the fright trigger has had a stepper since M4 because *"rolling the
  gentlest end … would quietly turn their failures into successes"*.
- **The book's own worked rituals use the far ends.** `GoldenRitualTest`
  accepts a worked row when `row.value == it.modifier || row.value ==
  it.best`, for both tables — so Section VIII prints rituals at values this
  dialog cannot produce.
- **`best` on all three classes has no production reader**, only tests that
  pin it was extracted.

It overturns a recorded decision, so it wants its decomposition reviewed
before code (the engine needs a validated pick on two tables; `Weak +0 to
-1` runs downward from a zero default; and a Full ritual refuses a link
outright). Not built here.

**Four of the eight instruments had no control when the table above was
first written**, which made the handover's "each recorded with its control"
false. They have one now, each a single planted line: `x = "\d"` appended to
a copy of a tools file returns `WARN invalid escape sequence`; a scratch test
calling `warnings.warn` surfaces in pytest's summary; `assert "Foo" in
s.lower()` is listed by the case-fold grep; `assert "→" in json.dumps(x)` is
counted as the one non-ASCII needle of one. The first attempt at that last
check had died on `grep -P` in this locale and printed nothing, which read
exactly like a clean result.

The other direction left open is the one the census only bounded — a
negative assertion whose needle cannot occur for a reason OTHER than case or
escaping, found by accident two slices running and by query in neither.

## 6ed. The file every citation is read against had no writer

6ec closed by naming a sweep nobody had run: *does a committed generated file
still reproduce from the tool that writes it?* This is that sweep, run over
everything in the tree a tool writes, and the guard that makes it stop being
a one-off.

**The sweep is clean, and it is recorded with its control.** Run on
2026-10-06 against `baf9df7`:

| Tool | Writes | Rewritten | Differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 40 `extract_*.py` | 81 content JSON | 81 of 81, one writer each | 0 |
| `extract_sheets.py` | 23 fixtures | 23 of 23 | 0 |
| `extract_pdf.py` | `pages.json`, `chapters.json` | 2 of 2 | 0 |
| `coverage.py` | `lines.json`, `coverage.md` | 2 of 2 | 0 |
| `extract_markdown.py` | `book.md` | 1 of 1 | 0 |
| `gen_theme.py` | `ThemeSchemes.kt` | 1 of 1 | 0 |

Each extractor was run from the committed tree on its own, which is enough:
every output equals its committed copy, so the set is a fixed point and no
run order can produce anything else. The query, for the content half:

```bash
for f in tools/extract_*.py; do   # minus extract_pdf, _markdown, _sheets
  touch marker; sleep 1; py $f
  find . -newer marker -type f    # what it WROTE
  git status --short              # what DIFFERS
done
```

**A zero from `git status` is not a zero until the same loop has returned
non-zero** (6ec). The control: overwrite exactly the files an extractor wrote
with `{"entries": []}`, re-run it, and require a clean tree. All 40 recover.
That is what turns "nothing changed" into "it rewrote 81 files and they came
out the same".

**The first upstream measurement was the instrument, and fixing it is what
found the slice.** I ran `extract_pdf.py` and byte-compared all six files in
`build/extract` against a backup: six lines of `same`. `extract_pdf` writes
TWO of them. The other four compared equal because nothing had touched them —
a failed generator's output looks exactly like a reproduced one (6cx, 6dk),
and so does the output of a generator that was never run. Re-done with an
mtime marker per tool, five of the six come out `NEW same` and one comes out
`old` under every tool in the directory:

**`build/extract/book.txt` had no writer.** It is the file this handover
calls the citation anchor — `<globalLineNumber>: <text>`, what every
`sourceLines` number is read against, what two tests open and what the QA
harness tells its models to grep. Its mtime is 2026-08-15, and no commit ever
gave it a writer: `git log --all -S"book.txt" -- tools qa-findings` returns
three commits and all three add READERS.
`extract_markdown.py` credited it to `extract_pdf.py` twice — once in its
docstring, once in the message it prints when the file is absent, *"run
extract_pdf.py first"* — and `extract_pdf.py` writes `pages.json` and
`chapters.json` and nothing else. So on a fresh clone the anchor could not be
built, and the tool that noticed would have named the wrong fix.

It is 6dg's sweep inverted: that one checked every content file for a
LOADER, this one checks every generated file for a WRITER. **It had not
drifted** — rendered from `lines.json` it matches on 10252 of 10252 lines —
so this is a missing producer (6cf), not a wrong number. `coverage.py` writes
it now, in the same walk of `pages.json` that numbers `lines.json`, because
two files that must carry one numbering should not be numbered twice. The
result is byte-identical to the hand-made file, CRLF and missing final
newline included.

**`extract_spirit.py` exited 1 after writing its file.** Its closing echo
quotes the book, the book prints `→`, and a redirected stdout on Windows is
cp1252. On a console it is fine, which is why it survived: every scripted run
— `py a.py && py b.py`, or an agent's shell — saw a failure, and this repo's
own rule that *a crashed extractor never rewrites its JSON* (6dk) then reads
`spirit_damage.json` as stale when it had just been rewritten correctly. One
line, `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")`, and the RED proof is the
redirected command itself: rc 1, then rc 0.

**Three tests ship, and the fixture is the design.** Each extractor is run
as a SCRIPT through `runpy`, with `Path.write_text` captured rather than
performed and stdout replaced by a strict cp1252 stream:

- `test_every_extractor_finishes_on_a_redirected_stdout` — RED on
  `extract_spirit`'s `UnicodeEncodeError`.
- `test_every_content_file_is_what_exactly_one_extractor_writes_today` — one
  comparison with four ways to fail: no writer, two writers, a stale file, a
  written file that is not there.
- `test_the_citation_anchor_is_what_coverage_writes_today` — RED on
  `book.txt` being absent from what `coverage.py` writes.

**The first version called `main()` and reported nine files with no writer.**
Four extractors (`extract_core_rules`, `extract_glossary`,
`extract_spirit_vision`, `extract_spirituality`) have no `main` at all — the
work is in the `if __name__ == "__main__":` body. That was the guard
measuring its own assumption, and `runpy.run_path(..., run_name="__main__")`
is the fix because it is also the more honest test: it runs what `py
tools/x.py` runs.

**The reproduction test passed the moment it was written, so its RED proof
is historical.** A worktree at `5e803b6` — the commit before 6ec's two fixes —
with the new tests dropped in names exactly three files:

```
{'non_standard_pathways.json': ['extract_non_standard'],
 'pathways.json': ['extract_pathways'],
 'pool_thresholds.json': ['extract_pools']}
```

Those are the three 6ec found by reading a regeneration diff line by line and
then by reading `b1c8c4e`'s file list. The third call site took 6ec a second
pass to find; the guard names it in under five seconds. The no-writer branch
is mutation-proved separately: a stray `zzz_hand_authored.json` in the content
directory fails it as `{'zzz_hand_authored.json': []}`.

**One thing the guard is stricter about than 6ec was.** 6ec called
`non_standard_pathways.json`'s change set-identical with no content change
(`[[a,b],[b+1,c]]` merging to `[[a,c]]`). The guard compares TEXT, so it
reports that file too. That is deliberate: "equal as line sets" is
`coverage.py`'s question (4.6), and "is this the file the tool writes" is this
one's.

**Bounds, stated.** `extract_pdf`, `extract_markdown` and `extract_sheets` are
not in the suite because their inputs are a PDF and 23 spreadsheets outside
the repo, and `gen_theme.py`'s docstring refuses wiring for its own reason (a
third-party colour dependency). Their rows above are a hand run and expire.
The content guard compares against the LOCAL `build/extract/lines.json`, so
it proves the JSON reproduces from the extraction on this machine;
`pages.json` → `lines.json` + `book.txt` is pinned by the third test, and PDF
→ `pages.json` is the hand run. Line endings are not pinned: the comparison
reads text, and this checkout has `core.autocrlf=true`.

**The fresh-clone case was run, not argued.** With `build/extract` moved
away the suite is 355 passed and 1 skipped (`book.md`, which only
`extract_markdown.py` builds): the `needs_pdf` tests near the top of the file
run `extract_pdf.py` and `coverage.py` as subprocesses, so the suite rebuilds
its own input, and all five rebuilt files — `book.txt` among them — are
byte-identical to the originals. Before this slice that run could not have
passed, because nothing would have written `book.txt` for the two tests that
open it. The bound is the PDF: with neither it nor `build/extract`, those
tests skip and nearly every other test in the file fails on `lines.json`,
the three new ones included — which predates this slice and is not changed by
it. One exit-code hole was looked for and is closed: `runpy` sees a nonzero
exit only as `SystemExit`, and `extract_content.py` is the one entry point
that calls a bare `main()` — whose body has no `return` at all.

**Writing `book.txt`'s format down found an assertion that could not fire.**
`test_spirit_vision_prints_rows_chapter_four_does_not` asserted `"
Critical
"
not in book` to show the short label is unique to 7.6's table. Every line of
`book.txt` opens with its own number, so that substring cannot occur whatever
the book prints — and the assertion read backwards besides: the bare label IS
printed, exactly once, at line 4850, inside 7.6's own span. It asserts that
now (`bare == [4850]`, and 4850 within `sourceLines`). Nobody had reason to
look, because the file's format was a fact about a hand-made artefact and
written down nowhere.

**The diff review (Codex, `codex exec`, three questions) returned no HIGH and
no MEDIUM.** Its checks are worth more than its findings: all 40 extractors
grep-verified to write through `Path.write_text` with no `newline=` or
`errors=` override, so the capture sees what lands on disk; and the 40 run in
forward AND reverse order to identical output for all 81 files, which is the
fixed-point argument measured instead of argued. Two LOWs:

- *Runs leak `sys.path`* — `extract_non_standard.py:36` inserts into it.
  **Taken**: the fixture snapshots `sys.path` per run. Its other half, evicting
  the modules a run imports, is **refused**: they are the same `extract_pathways`
  and `coverage` the suite imports by name, and evicting them leaves two copies
  of one module in a process, which is the worse leak.
- *`reconfigure` raises on a stream that has none (`io.StringIO`)* —
  **refused**, with the bound stated. A script run always has a
  `TextIOWrapper`; the only in-process callers are tests, and no test calls
  `extract_spirit.main()`. A `hasattr` guard is a branch nothing reaches.

It also named a bound this slice does not close: a diagnostic on a branch the
committed data never takes (`extract_non_standard.py:148`) can still print an
unencodable character, and no run over committed data can prove otherwise.
**The Critical-line assertion and the `sys.path` line landed AFTER that
review** (6dl: a verdict expires when the diff moves under it); both are
test-only, and the suite is 356 green with them.

**No successor is named.** Writer-for-every-generated-file is closed and
guarded. What the guard cannot see is its own input: PDF → `pages.json` runs
by hand, and nothing notices a `build/extract` built from a different PDF
than the one the committed JSON came from, except that the content test would
then fail on every file at once.

## 6ec. One sentence, arriving as two wrong fields

**The sweep this slice set out to run came back clean, and the defect was
found beside it.** The direction was the inverse of 6ea's: 6ea checked every
content JSON KEY for a Kotlin declaration, and this checked every declared
`@Serializable` property for a JSON key that actually SETS it. A property no
data file populates is always its default, so anything reading it reads a
constant — 6ea's defect class and 6dz's, at a third unit.

**The first run of it measured the instrument, not the data.** Matching every
property name against the union of all 81 files' keys returned **0 of 471**,
because a key named `name` exists in nearly every file. Tightened to match
each class against only the file(s) that decode into it, it returned 10 — and
its loader mapping silently covered **73 of 81 files**, because the regex
required the `load(...)` call to sit directly under `by lazy {` and eight of
them have a comment in between. Widened to track the enclosing property type
line by line: **81 of 81, every root a known class, 10 hits.** A sweep that
skips ten per cent of its corpus and still reports a number is the shape this
repo keeps recording.

**All ten are settled, each by its own named query rather than by assertion:**

| Hit | Query | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `advantages.json`: `SelfControlRoll`'s four fields, and `TraitDefinition.selfControl` | `\(\d+\)` over each catalogue's claimed spans | **0 in the advantages spans, 9 in the disadvantages spans** (`Curious (12)`, `Greed (12)`, …). The book prints no self-control ADVANTAGE, so the field is correctly absent |
| `disadvantages.json`: `TraitDefinition.perLevel`, `variableCost` | `level`/`variable`/`scales`/`per ` over the 402 lines of the disadvantages spans | 3 matches, none a PRICE (`Bad Temper (12)`, a once-per-session clause, a cumulative Will penalty). No per-level or variable-cost disadvantage exists to drop. `costMin`/`costMax` ARE set there — 13 rows — so ranges are captured |
| `ritual_quick_preparation.json`: `RitualPreparation.openEnded` | book line 4064 | prints `-2 to -4`, a bounded range. Only the FULL table's `None` row prints `-4 or worse`, and it carries the flag |
| `non_standard_pathways.json`: `SkillGrant.note`, `StatGain.note` | a gain-line qualifier regex, **run first over `pathways.json`'s spans as a positive control** | 10 hits there against 12 stored notes, so the query fires; **0 over chapters 14/15**. Those blocks print no qualifier |

**The positive control is the reusable part.** My first version of that
qualifier query returned 0 over chapters 14/15 AND 0 over `pathways.json`,
which holds twelve stored notes — so the 0 settled nothing. It failed because
the flattened PDF puts the attribute on one line and its gain on the next,
and the regex was anchored on the attribute. **A sweep's zero is worth nothing
until the same query has returned non-zero on data known to contain the
thing.**

**What the control turned up is the slice.** Of the ten qualifier lines it
found, one is ability prose (White Tower Seq 6, line 8226, a false positive
of the regex) and one does not wrap at all (Death Seq 7's `+2 (upgrade)`).
Eight wrap onto a following line; **six carry their continuation into the
stored note and two lost it**:

- **White Tower Seq 9** (book 5640-5641). The book prints `IQ +1 (knowledge
  retention and learning)`. Stored: the stat note was `"(knowledge retention"`
  — an unclosed bracket — and the tail landed at the END of the advantages
  blob, which read `"Eidetic Memory +5 to remember things after one reading;
  near-perfect recall and learning)"`.
- **Demoness Seq 9** (book 5811-5812). The book prints `Basic Speed +0.25 —
  reflexes sharpen for precise timing`. Stored: the note was `"— reflexes
  sharpen"` and the advantages blob OPENED `"for precise timing Night Vision
  …"`.

**One sentence, arriving as two wrong fields**, and both fields render:
`PathwayScreen.kt:505` prints `gain.note` and `:513` prints
`Prose(block.advantages)`.

**The signal is the book's own, and it is measured.** A wrapped line is the
middle of a sentence, so it opens lowercase; the next row's name is a proper
noun and does not. Over every block this parser sees — the 88 potion blocks
AND the 17 non-standard ones, because `extract_non_standard.py` calls the same
function — **62 lines follow a stat gain line inside the Stat / Advantage
section, 60 open with a capital and are advantage names (`Eidetic Memory`,
`Acute Vision`, `Fit`, `Perfect Balance`, …), and the 2 that do not are
exactly these two remainders.** Zero false positives over the whole corpus.
The first version of that count said 88 blocks and 53/2/51; the diff review's
LOW was that the 17 non-standard blocks use the same parser and were excluded
from the corpus that could contradict the rule — **an assertion's corpus
excluding the rows that could disagree**, 6dn's shape. Re-run over all 105: 9
more followers, all uppercase.

**Two other anchors were refused and the reasons matter.** Balancing
parentheses fixes White Tower and cannot reach Demoness, whose em-dash
qualifier has no closing token. Looking the following line up in
`advantages.json` fails on the very case that needs it: the book writes
`Night Vision` and the catalogue prints `Night Eyes`. **The extractor's own
docstring records why neither works in general** — "no textual signal
separates a wrapped effect line from the next row's name",
`Sunlight/purification/holy` against `Poison Resistance` — and that claim is
about an ADVANTAGE row's boundary and still stands. The docstring says so now
rather than reading as contradicted, and it names its own counter-example as
the other direction: a capitalised continuation is left where it falls.

**Regenerating found the second defect, which is larger.** `b1c8c4e`
("partition chapters at the heading, not the page") taught `coverage.py` that
a chapter starts at its HEADING, because the book opens a chapter mid-page and
the page furniture above that heading belongs to the chapter before it. That
commit hand-refiled `pathways.json`'s spans to match. **`extract_pathways.py`
was never taught**, and still bucketed claimed lines by `chapters.json` page
ranges — so re-running it silently re-filed three spans back to the defect,
each of them a `"Powered by GURPS: Pathways"` furniture line at the top of the
next chapter's first page. **One question, two sites, one taught** — and this
one is armed, because the only thing between it and the repo is someone
reading a regeneration diff.

**The fix is to ask the question once.** `chapter_at(n, heading_of)` is the
last chapter whose heading precedes a line, and `heading_of_chapters` asks
`coverage.heading_lines` rather than restating it — which also inherits that
function's refusal to fall back to the page range when a heading cannot be
found. **The signature change is what found the second call site**:
`extract_non_standard.py` shares `extract()` and failed loudly with a
`TypeError` rather than quietly keeping the old answer.

**A THIRD site was found by reading `b1c8c4e`'s own file list, and it is
the worst of them.** That commit refiled three content files, not two:
`pool_thresholds.json` moved lines 2346-2356 from chapter 5 to chapter 4.
`extract_pools.py` did not bucket by page — it had `CHAPTER = "5"`, a
constant, and wrote BOTH printed ranges under it. The SPI ladder prints in
chapter 4 (Spirituality, heading at 2247) and only the HP one is chapter
5's (heading 2361), so a re-run put the refile straight back — confirmed by
running it. **A hardcoded answer cannot learn a correction**, and nothing
in the file said where the number came from. `chapter_spans` asks the same
`chapter_at`, and a range no heading precedes RAISES rather than returning
None, which would have written the key as JSON `null`. The regenerated file
is set-identical to `HEAD`; only the key ORDER moves, because the ranges are
now iterated in the file's own ascending line order. The fourth two-line
header `b1c8c4e` names is `non_standard_pathways.json`'s `[9323,9324]`.

**"Is there a fourth site?" is answered by an audit, not by a grep, and
the grep is why.** `grep -l 'chapters.json|startPage'` over `tools/` does
NOT return `extract_pools.py` — a hardcoded `CHAPTER = "5"` is invisible
to it, which is the worst form of this defect and the one that query cannot
see. So the audit asks the DATA: every chapter key of every top-level
`sourceLines` dict in all 81 committed files, checked against
`chapter_at`. **80 files carry one, and 0 spans disagree** — so
`extract_core_rules.py`'s own hardcoded constant is right rather than
merely unexamined. It ships as a test, with the pre-`b1c8c4e`
`pool_thresholds` span as an inline positive control, and it is also the
only thing that would catch `extract_pools.main()` being reverted to a
hardcoded key: `chapter_spans` is unit-tested and nothing else asserts
`main` calls it — the same gap the `extract()` signature change closed by
accident.

**The oracle for that half was the committed file itself.** Chapter headings
sit at 5416 / 6217 / 7043 / 8098 / 8908, and `HEAD`'s spans end at 6216, 7042,
8097 and 8905 — exactly heading-partitioned, because `b1c8c4e` did it by hand.
The regenerated spans are byte-different and **set-identical**: the per-line
loop no longer breaks a block where the chapter key changed, so
`[[5466,6166],[6167,6216]]` becomes `[[5466,6216]]`. The printed per-chapter
counts (751 / 820 / 1049 / 803) match `HEAD` exactly, and `coverage.py`
compares line SETS, never ranges (4.6). `non_standard_pathways.json` merged the
same way with no content change.

**The partition half is pinned by a test that RED-proves against the old
behaviour, not merely against a missing function.** The first version of
`test_a_line_above_a_mid_page_chapter_heading...` exercised `chapter_at`
alone, and `test_a_block_stops_at_the_next_chapter_heading`'s fixture had
the page boundary and the heading on the same line — so reverting
`chapter_of` to page bucketing left all 351 tests green, which is the exact
silent revert this slice exists to stop. **An `AttributeError` proves a
function is missing, not that a behaviour changed.** That fixture now puts
a chapter 9 line on chapter 10's PAGE, the way 6167 sits in the book, and
the mutation fails it with the defect's own shape
(`{'10': [[3, 3], [6, 8]]}`).

**Two corpus guards ship, and each RED-proved on a DIFFERENT instance.**
Against the committed pre-fix JSON,
`test_no_pathway_string_is_cut_mid_parenthetical` names White Tower and
`test_no_pathway_prose_field_opens_mid_sentence` names Demoness. They are not
redundant: an em-dash wrap strands no bracket, and a bracket wrap that lands at
the END of the prose blob leaves it opening with a capital. Both read the
**committed file** rather than entries built in memory, because a crashed
extractor never rewrites its JSON (6dk). The diff review called them vacuous —
deleting the fix leaves them green until someone regenerates — which is **true
and is what the unit test is for**; each docstring says which half it covers,
rather than a third copy of the check being added.

**One review finding is refused with the chain that closes it.** The reviewer
wanted `in_scope` filtered by `chapter_at` as well, on the grounds that a line
the headings put outside chapters 9-12 is still walked. It cannot be claimed
wrongly: a chapter heading INSIDE the walked pages already bounds the block
(`end = min(end, next_heading - 1)`), one outside them is past the last walked
line (chapter 13's heading is 8908 on p. 144; chapter 12's pages end at 143 and
the last claimed line is 8905), and `heading_lines` RAISES rather than falling
back if a heading cannot be found. A filter there is a guard that cannot fire.

**Device-verified on an SM-T570 without drinking anything**, because the
pathway screen renders a block before the Drink button is tapped. Academic
Researcher, Demoness Seq 9: `Basic Speed +0.25` over `— reflexes sharpen for
precise timing`, and Advantages opening `Night Vision see in total darkness
…`. White Tower Seq 9: `IQ +1` over `(knowledge retention and learning)`, and
Advantages ending `… near-perfect recall`. Both halves of both instances, on
the screen that shows them.

**Gradle failed once more with the Windows lock**, this time as `Failed to
clean up stale outputs` on `:core:rules:processResources` rather than `Unable
to delete directory`. Same fix, same indistinguishability from a real failure:
`rm -rf` the module's `build/resources` and re-run.

**No successor is named.** The property sweep is closed and recorded above, and
the next slice needs a fresh direction. One thing found on the way and NOT
chased: the committed `pathways.json` did not reproduce from a fresh local
build before this slice, and the only reason anyone would notice is reading a
regeneration diff line by line. There is no check anywhere that a committed
content file still reproduces — every extractor writes its file and nothing
compares the file to what the extractor would write today. That is a sweep
direction, and it is the one this slice was saved by.

## 6eb. The parry the sheet screen could never show

**One question, answered at two sites, with data at one.**
`DefenseDialog.armedParries` read `Character.weapons` and computed each row
with `ParryBlock.parryFor`. No published sheet prints a weapon row — a grep
for `weapons` across `fixtures/` returns nothing — and no `SavedEdits` field
could write one, so **the armed-parry rows were permanently absent on all 23
premades**. One tap away, `AttackDialog.kt:722` has printed
`Weapons.parryFor(held.weapon, skillLevel)` for a chapter-8 weapon since that
catalogue was read. So a character could swing a Broadsword and could not
parry with it, and the function's own KDoc said *"No premade carries a weapon
today, so nothing here is on screen yet"* — a gap recorded in the place only
its author reads.

This is the second of the two gaps 6dz recorded and called features rather
than oversights; 6ea closed the other. Both were fields whose only writer was
somebody else's data.

Read it for six things.

**The load-bearing decision was the SHAPE, and the design review took it.**
`armedParries` moves from `List<Weapon>` to `List<CataloguedWeapon>` and
computes with `Weapons.parryFor`. `Weapon.parryMod` exists because a
published SHEET prints a dash or a number beside a weapon row; `Weapons.kt`'s
own KDoc records that this book prints **no per-weapon parry modifier
anywhere**, leaving `ParryBlock.parryFor` *"for the sheets that carry one"*.
Manufacturing `Weapon(name, skill, parryMod = if (canParry) 0 else null)`
from catalogue data would claim chapter 8 supplied a modifier it never
printed, invent a `SkillKey`'s difficulty and controlling attribute out of a
printed skill STRING, and leave two formulas for one fact agreeing only by
construction. **The strongest case against it is recorded rather than
dismissed**: a future importer carrying a fencing blade at +1 would get no
defence row, so `ParryBlock.parryFor` and `Character.weapons` are a stated
non-goal in production source — *"No production caller today, and that is a
scope decision rather than dead code"* — not accidental silence.

**The tests MOVED rather than died, and that is the honest artefact.**
`ParryBlock.parryFor` and `Weapon.parryMod` were pinned by exactly one thing
in this repo: five `armedParries` cases in `DefenseDialogTest`, three of
which asserted the modifier. Switching the screen's shape would have deleted
the only proof that the sheet path's formula is right. The three cases are
rewritten as one `ParryBlockTest` case instead, where they belong — **a
formula with no test is a claim** — and the remaining four become
catalogue-based.

**Possession is not training, and the design review is what settled it.** My
decomposition offered the picker only the weapons the character's own skills
can wield. That makes possession require training, which neither the book nor
this app says: a GM may hand anyone a weapon. All nine rows are offered, and a
weapon no skill arms prints *"not a skill this character has, so no parry"*
rather than vanishing — **a saved weapon that renders nowhere is
indistinguishable from a save that lost it.** The reviewer's further point is
recorded and REFUSED with its counter-case: it wanted `AttackDialog`'s weapon
chips filtered to possessed weapons too, or else *"Defense says possession
matters while Attack does not"*. Filtering them would withdraw a working
capability for want of a record the app has only just gained. The distinction
is 6cx's, and it is about ROLE: Attack's chips are a PICKER that
re-parameterises one roll and is answered per roll; the defence rows are a
LIST rendered with no choice, so they need a possession record to know which
rows to print. **A picker asks; a list asserts.**

**`levelFor` takes the HIGHEST matching level, never the first.** p. 85 makes
two rows of one name at two difficulties into two different skills, and five
of this book's potion grants produce exactly that, so a `skillLevels` map can
legitimately hold `Knife/Easy` and `Knife/Average` at once and iteration order
would otherwise decide the number. The join runs through `forSkill`, the
direction that already exists and the one that reads the specialization —
going the other way means parsing `"Guns (Revolver)"` back into a `SkillKey`
and inventing the two fields the catalogue never printed.

**The diff review returned four findings and all four were the vacuity
class.** Three are RED-proved by mutation. The first MEDIUM is the sharpest:
deleting `+ parryPenalty` from the ARMED rows alone left every test green,
because `DefenseDialogTest` exercises `armedParries`' base values and nothing
composes the row. The two row types differ by exactly one term (an unarmed
style parries a WEAPON at its own penalty), so they are now one `parryScore`
expression with that term defaulted — **one question, one site**, which is the
defect this slice is about, one screen further in. **No test pins the sum,
because a test of `a + b + c` restates it**; what stops the drift is that
there is one expression, and whether the screen calls it with the right
arguments is only reachable on a device. The second MEDIUM: my "highest level"
test inserted the 14 LAST, so *"take the last match"* passed it — both map
orders are asserted now, and the mutation that proves it is `lastOrNull`,
where my own first mutation had been `firstOrNull` and told me nothing. The
two LOWs are the same shape in the case-insensitive matches: a dedupe test
whose repeat simply vanished behind the canonical entry ahead of it, and a
drop test that used the canonical spelling for both calls. **A test written
for a rule about SPELLING must use a spelling the code has to normalise.**

**Device-verified on an SM-T570 on 2026-09-27, in the session after the one
that shipped it.** All three claims held. The carrier was the Journalist,
which carries no Knife at all, so the untrained line and the granted one are
the SAME row read twice: as a mortal it printed *"Knife — not a skill this
character has, so no parry"* with the defence dialog showing no armed row at
all, and after one Error Sequence 9 potion (*Marauder*: DX +1, then Knife at
DX/Easy +3) it printed **"Knife 13 — parry 9"**. The defence dialog one tap
away printed **`Parry (Combat Knife) 9`** — **one expression, two screens,
one number**, which is 3f177c5's check rather than one of this slice's
three, and the one reading the pre-fix code would have failed. The picker
offered **all nine catalogue rows** — five firearms and four melee — to a
character trained in none of them, marking the taken one
*"· carried"*; the budget stayed at 91 of 100, because a weapon costs no
points. The cumulative penalty ran `9` to `5` on one prior parry, with the
note moving from *"The first parry of a round is free"* to *"Parry rows above
include −4"*, and `New round` put both back. And the carry survived an
`am force-stop`: `sessions.json` holds `"weapons": ["Combat Knife"]` — the
catalogue NAME, as designed — beside the Error block, and the row read back
`Knife 13 — parry 9` on relaunch. **The additive widening is proved by the
saves that predate it**: the two entries written before this field existed
loaded without loss.

**One thing the pass found outside the slice, recorded and not repaired.**
`PremadeGallery.isBeyonder` is `sheet.published.spi > 0`, so a character the
player walks onto a pathway keeps its `Mortal` tab and its `SPI 0` in the
roster while the sheet one tap away says otherwise. That is not this slice's
defect and it may not be a defect at all — every number in a gallery row is
the PUBLISHED sheet's, attributes included, so the screen is internally
consistent and nothing says it is meant to show live state. It wants its own
reading before anyone calls it the one-question-two-sites shape.

**One environment fact worth inheriting.** Gradle failed six times in this
session with `java.io.IOException: Unable to delete directory` on
`build/test-results`, `build/kotlin` and `build/intermediates` — a Windows
file lock, and **it is indistinguishable from a build failure in the exit
code**. The fix each time was `rm -rf` on the directory the message names,
plus `--no-watch-fs`; nothing about the code was wrong. Read the message,
not the status.

**A third finding landed after the diff review, and it is this slice's own
defect one layer up.** `MainActivity` has built the LIVE skill levels since
M3 — a potion's grants folded in — under a comment saying they are *"computed
once for defence, attack and the ritual gate rather than three times over"*.
The builder's new Weapons row computed its own from `Derive` alone, which is
the PURCHASED character, so **a Beyonder whose potion granted the weapon's
skill would read one parry beside the weapon they carry and another on the
defence screen, from one save.** One question, two sites, in the slice that
exists to remove an instance of exactly that. `liveSkillLevels(character)` is
the one expression now and both screens call it. The builder's OTHER rows
keep `derived`, correctly: the budget bills purchases and a grant is free
(M3). Found by asking what the variable at the older call site actually held
rather than by reading the one I had just written — **I asserted the new
screen's choice and never checked the old screen's.**

**And the docs pass found a slice with no section in this file.**
`CLAUDE.md` went back over its 150 k-char limit (152,583), so the lead
paragraphs for 6cz down to 6cd were cut — every one of them duplicated in
full here, and the reading order still names them. Checked before cutting,
one `grep -c` per slice, and **22 of 23 were present**: 6ct's section had
never been written, so that paragraph was its only surviving account. It is
restored above as its own section, quoting the paragraph verbatim rather than
reconstructing work it did not witness. **A lead paragraph can be the only
copy** — 6cp's rule was that a closing paragraph is the one part of this log
nothing verifies, and this is the same hazard one file over.

**1732 Kotlin** (1227 `core:rules`, 485 `app`, 20 `core:model`) and **347
Python**, all green, counted from the JUnit XML after deleting the results
directories. Chapter coverage is untouched: nothing here claims a book line.

**No successor is named.** Both gaps 6dz recorded are now closed, so the next
slice needs a fresh sweep, and every direction already run expires rather
than standing: fields for a reader (6ai), functions for a caller (6cf), rows
for a consumer (6ci), files for a loader (6dg), strings a screen types (6cq),
seams between claimed spans (6ba), what the tests know that production does
not (6bz), parameters with no non-default argument (6dz), JSON keys with no
Kotlin declaration and enum members with no production use (6ea). The one
thing outstanding is not a sweep but a device pass over this slice.

## 6ea. Six rows the budget billed and no screen could ask for

**6dz closed its census with a verdict and named no successor, so this slice
began with two fresh sweeps.** Both came back clean and both are recorded with
their bounds, because a sweep that finds nothing still has a deliverable (6de)
and an instrument's reach is the part that expires.

| Sweep | Unit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| every KEY in every content JSON checked for a Kotlin declaration | JSON key | **clean** — 81 files, one hit (`glossary.json`'s `"G"`, a chapter label inside `sourceLines`, not a field) |
| every enum MEMBER checked for a production use | enum entry | **clean** — 116 members, 35 flagged and every one a false positive |

The first is a direction this repo had not run and it has a real failure mode:
`ContentLoader` builds its decoder with `ignoreUnknownKeys = true`
(`ContentLoader.kt:14`), so a key an extractor writes that no `@Serializable`
class declares is **dropped in silence at decode** — invisible to 6ai's
fields-for-a-reader sweep, which iterates Kotlin declarations and therefore
cannot see a key that never becomes one. **State its bound rather than the
count**: the query matched the key as a word against all of `src/main`, so a
key spelled like an unrelated Kotlin word (`name`, `cost`) passes on that word
alone. The second sweep's 35 flags are the instrument too — it excluded the
whole DECLARING file, so every member a picker reaches through `entries` (five
`ThemeSeed`s, `Incoming`, `SheetTab`) reads as unused. Neither number is a
finding; both are a measurement of the query.

**What shipped came from 6dz's own closing paragraph, which named two real
gaps and called them features.** `Character.secondaryDelta` is one of them:
`PointBudget.report` has taken it and charged
`SecondaryCharacteristics.costOf` since M0, `Derive` composes it,
`PotionDigestion` adds grants into it — and **nothing in production ever
constructed a non-default one**, so the six rows chapter 2 prices on pp. 8-9
(HP ±2, FP ±3, Will ±5, Per ±5, Basic Speed ±5 per 0.25, Basic Move ±5) could
be billed and never bought. The engine could charge for them and no screen
could ask. That is 6dz's own defect class — a parameter with no non-default
argument — one rung up, at a FIELD whose only writer was a potion.

Read it for six things.

**The save stores the book's row key, not the object the engine bills.**
`SavedEdits.secondaries` is a `Map<String, Int>` — `"hp"`, `"basicSpeed"` —
because `SecondaryDelta`'s `init` rejects a magnitude over 100 and
`SessionStore.load` discards the WHOLE file on a decode failure, so one
hand-edited number would delete every other edit a player had made. That is
the same rule `wealth`, `appearance` and `traits` already follow: a save NAMES
and the book RESOLVES. The design review's condition on accepting it is
recorded in the field's KDoc — those keys are stable save identifiers from
here on, so renaming a row in `secondary_costs.json` stops applying every save
that named it, silently — and it corrected the argument I had written for it:
*"a map cannot throw at decode"* is too strong, since a wrong JSON value type
still loses the file. It avoids exactly one throw, the constructor's.

**The merge ADDS and the reason is a state, not a preference.** My
decomposition proposed replacing `base.secondaryDelta` when the map is
non-empty, on the evidence that no fixture carries a non-zero delta (checked,
not assumed — a grep for the field across `fixtures/` returns nothing). The
review named the state that breaks it: a potion grants Will +1, the player
buys a point of HP, and a sparse map naming one row zeroes the granted Will.
**A reachability claim about today's fixtures is not an argument about the
API**, and `PotionDigestion` is the caller that proves it — it has been adding
into this field since M3.

**One key→field table, and the pin test keeps its own.** `stepsOf`,
`withSteps`, `plusSteps` and `valueLabelOf` all live in
`SecondaryCharacteristics`, so the stepper, the resolver and the value shown
beside it ask one authority rather than each carrying a copy (6dv). The
obvious tidy-up — rewriting `SecondaryCostPinTest.engineCostOf` to call the
new mapping — was **refused by the design review with the arithmetic that
settles it**: four of the six rows cost 5 points, so a mapping that sent Will,
Per, Basic Speed and Basic Move to one field would satisfy that test's price
loop unchanged. The test's independent `when` is the oracle and stays.

**The diff review's two MEDIUMs were one line, and the device had already
printed the proof.** `SecondaryRow` first carried a *"sheet prints 4.50"*
comparison derived from the unedited CHARACTER — the engine's own derivation,
not the sheet's printed column — and at least 19 of the 23 sheets floor Basic
Speed where the book does not. The Vitals screen one tap away reads
**`Basic Speed 4.50 (sheet: 4.00)`** for that very row, so the line would have
asserted the opposite of the recorded disagreement on the majority of the
corpus. Its second MEDIUM is the same line from the other side: gating the
comparison on `steps != 0` hides a potion-granted value that also differs.
**Both die by deleting the claim rather than repairing it** —
`SheetComparison` is the authority for computed-versus-published and it
renders correctly one tap away, so a copy here was a third printing of a
number (6cr). What ships says what this screen can back:
`±2 pts per level — +1 bought`.

**The third MEDIUM is an overflow the bound could not catch.** `plusSteps`
folded the saved steps onto the carried ones and coerced afterwards, so a
hand-edited `Int.MAX_VALUE` plus any positive grant wraps negative and lands
inside ±100 as a legal purchase. The saved operand is coerced BEFORE the
addition now. **A bound applied after arithmetic is not a bound on the
arithmetic.**

**Four of the five LOWs were vacuity and all four bit.** Three are RED-proved
by mutation: `valueLabelOf("hp")` reading `maxFp` (the original test used a
default character, where HP and FP are both 9 — so the assertion survived the
swap; the fixture now has six DISTINCT values), `plusSteps` replacing instead
of adding (the original test granted Will and bought HP, which the replacement
satisfies; it buys Will on top of granted Will now), and `setSecondary`
clearing to `emptyMap()` instead of removing the key (the original saved one
row, so emptying it looked identical; two rows are saved and one is cleared
now). The fourth added the lower bound to the setter's coercion test. **The
overflow fix above was itself untested for an hour**: the coercion test bought
against an EMPTY base, where no addition can overflow, so it passed whether
the operand was coerced before the sum or only after it — the fix for a
finding about guards that cannot fire, shipped with a guard that could not
fire. A carried step plus `Int.MAX_VALUE` is the case that discriminates, and
it is RED-proved. The
fifth asked for a Compose test of the stepper wiring and is refused on the
standing reason: no test in this repo can reach a composable, which is why the
rows below were read off a device. `?: return@items` became `checkNotNull`
with a message — unreachable while the content test holds, and a priced row
the mapping cannot label should fail loudly rather than vanish (6dy's
`requireNotNull`, same shape).

**Device-verified on an SM-T570, both directions.** Church Healer (ST 9, IQ
11, HT 9): the section renders six rows and only six — SPI, CoR and Digestion
carry no `pointsPerStep` and offer no stepper, which is the book's refusal
read off the data rather than a list of three names. Basic Speed **4.50 →
4.75** on one tap with the budget going **102 of 105, 3 spare → 107 of 105 —
over budget** in red: five points for one QUARTER, which is the unit the whole
parse turns on. Basic Move stayed 4 under it, because 4.75 still floors to 4.
HP **9 → 10** at 104 of 105, the sub-line reading `±2 pts per level — +1
bought`, and the sheet's own pool tracker one screen back reading **HP 10 /
10** while its comparison table still reads HP 9 — correct, and worth stating:
that table is `SheetComparison.of(sheet)`, keyed on the SHEET, so it stays the
engine-against-the-book diff a purchase must not move (6e). Stepping back to 9
cleared the line, the budget and the saved entry together, and the purchase
survived a reinstall before that.

**1723 Kotlin** (1223 `core:rules`, 480 `app`, 20 `core:model`) and **347
Python**, all green, counted from the JUnit XML after deleting the results
directories — a filtered run leaves only its own leftovers and the next plain
run reports UP-TO-DATE. Chapter coverage is untouched: nothing here claims a
book line, which is the fourth measurement that applying a rule and moving a
percentage are different things.

**No successor is named.** The gap this slice closes was one of the two 6dz
recorded, and the other — `Character.weapons`, what `ParryBlock` has been
waiting on since M0 — is now the only one of the two left. It needs the same
additive `SavedEdits` widening this slice just proved out, plus a picker over
`Weapons.all()`; that is a design review's question, not a sentence here. The
sweep directions that have now been run and expire rather than standing:
fields for a reader (6ai), functions for a caller (6cf), rows for a consumer
(6ci), files for a loader (6dg), strings a screen types (6cq), seams between
claimed spans (6ba), what the tests know that production does not (6bz),
parameters with no non-default argument (6dz), **JSON keys with no Kotlin
declaration** and **enum members with no production use** (6ea).

## 6dz. The sweep 6dy named, run — and a chip whose only effect was nothing

**6dy named a sweep and this is it: every optional parameter checked for a
non-default ARGUMENT.** 369 optional public parameters across `core/rules` and
`core/model`; 175 excluded by the query's own rules (a `ContentLoader` default
and a `RandomSource` are test seams this repo builds deliberately, and a
function with no production caller belongs to 6cf's sweep, not this one); of
the 194 left, **36 are never overridden in production and 5 are a real gap.**

**Two of the five are already-recorded deliberate gaps** — `Character.weapons`
and `Character.secondaryDelta`, both named in CLAUDE.md §6 as "not editable
yet". **One is a false positive and was checked rather than believed**:
`Ranged.modifiers(gmValue)` was reported as making the darkness severity
unreachable, and the screen does have a bespoke path for that row — but it is
`darknessCause`/`darknessReduction`, which is Night Eyes' RELIEF and not the
severity at all. So the finding was right about the gap and wrong about the
mechanism, which is 6cz's rule (take a reviewer's diagnosis over its
prescription) applied to a census.

**The two that ship are the same defect wearing two costumes.** Several of
this book's modifier rows print a SPAN rather than a number, and every engine
that reads one has taken a `gmValue: Map<String, Int>` override — validated
against the printed ends — since the row was extracted. **Only `BoonDialog`
ever passed one.** So:

- Ticking `Method match +0 to +2` on the divination screen applied **+0**. A
  control whose only effect is nothing, with its own range printed on it.
  Four rows on that table are like this (`+0 to +2`, `+0 to +4`, `-1 to -2`,
  `+0 to +1`), and `+0 to +4` is the largest single bonus the screen offers.
- `Darkness or heavy fog -3 to -9 depending on severity` was always **-3**,
  with the other six severities unreachable — on a screen that prints the
  range on the chip. `Ranged.reliefFor`'s own KDoc had already written down
  that "the GM's severity is the book's and stays inside the printed range",
  so the engine was waiting for a caller that never came.
- `Previous divination about the same subject (cumulative) -2 per repeat` is
  the same defect one layer down. `Divination.modifierTotal` multiplies by
  `repeats` and the screen never passed a count, so **a third attempt cost
  what the first did.**

**The helper is shared because the count of wrong ways was already two.**
`BoonDialog` had a private `endsOf` and the other two screens had nothing, so
a per-screen fix would leave three near-identical functions and a fourth
screen free to get it wrong a fourth way. `endsBetween(from, to)` is one
function in the app module, `endsOf` delegates to it, and **its order is the
load-bearing part**: it runs OUTWARD from the row's own figure, because a
descending span (`-1 to -2`, `-3 to -9`) worsens as it runs and numeric order
would put the WORST case first — leaving the chip the roll is actually using
at the far end of the row. Mutation-proved by swapping in `sorted()`: three
tests redden, including both that read the ends off the content.

**The default chip shows selected, and that is a claim about the engine.**
Nothing is picked until the GM picks, and what the engine applies until then
is `row.modifier` — so the chip rendered as selected on an untouched row is
the one the roll is using, rather than a UI default that happens to agree. The
screen passes an empty map rather than eagerly seeding `picked`, which keeps
one authority on that default and it is not the screen.

**A stale pick cannot reach a later roll**, and the guard is the one
`BoonDialog` already used: `overrides` is built by filtering `picked` against
the rows ticked RIGHT NOW, rather than by pruning `picked` on every change.
That is the defect the attack dialog's "Another turn" shipped with, avoided by
construction rather than by remembering to clean up.

**Device-verified on an SM-T570, on both screens.** Divination (Apothecary,
Hermit Sequence 9, Divination Arts 20): ticking `Method match` and `Previous
divination` gave `Roll 3d6 ≤ 16 — Skill 20, question +2, circumstances -6`,
which is -2 × 3 repeats with the method match still at its +0; picking **+2**
moved it to `≤ 18 … circumstances -4`. Attack, at range, darkness ticked:
`How bad is it?` offers -3 through -9 and picking -9 prints `Range and
cover: -9`. Before this slice neither number could move.

**The diff review returned four findings and every one was about a guard that
could not fire.** Codex hit its weekly limit mid-review and the free `pi-qa`
gateway was down, so this went through the single-agent fallback CLAUDE.md
names — one reviewer, three questions, the files needed to answer them.

- **The severity was a scene fact that outlived its scene.** "Another turn"
  clears the band, the circumstances, the aim and what the scene was lit by,
  under a comment saying that inheriting last turn's distance or cover would
  modify the next roll invisibly. The severity added in this slice was not
  added to that list, so pitch dark last turn priced this turn's dusk at -9.
  **The warrant is the file's own standard, not the value's invisibility** —
  every sibling on that list is equally visible as a selected chip and is
  reset anyway.
- **`endsBetween`'s `to == from` branch was dead**, because `(n downTo n)` is
  already `[n]`. The branch and the test written to guard it are both deleted:
  a branch no edit can change the output of is a comment pretending to be code.
- **The content census passed on an empty filter.** `every printed divination
  range is offered` looped over `Divination.modifiers().filter { it.best !=
  null }`, so a re-extraction dropping `best` from all four rows would have
  left it green and silent. The four are pinned by name before the loop now.
- **Nothing reached the wiring either screen exists for.** Deleting the
  `gmValue` argument from the attack dialog, or the overrides from the
  divination one, left every test green — the defect this slice is about,
  reproduced in the tests written for it. `rangedModifiers` is internal and
  `overridesFor` is extracted, each with a test RED-proved by neutering the
  one line it guards.

The four other stale-state paths were checked and are clean, and one of them
is worth inheriting: **not auto-incrementing `repeats` on "Ask again" is
correct**, because the row prices PREVIOUS divinations, which may have
happened off-screen, and bumping it would be the app authoring a clock it does
not hold (6dc's refusal, applied to a counter).

**The reset is device-verified too**, which is the only way it could be: tick
Darkness, pick -9, tap "Another turn", tick Darkness again — the row comes
back with **-3 selected and `Range and cover: -3`**. A `uiautomator` dump
cannot read it, because Compose does not expose a `FilterChip`'s selection as
the `checked` attribute the dump prints; the screencap is the instrument here
(6du's rule about taps, applied to a reading).

**1710 Kotlin** (1215 `core:rules`, 475 `app`, 20 `core:model`) and **347
Python**, all green. Chapter coverage is untouched, because nothing here
claims a book line — which is the third measurement that **applying a rule and
moving a percentage are different things** (6di, 6dk, 6dq).

**No successor is named, and that is a verdict rather than an omission.** 6cp's
rule is that a closing paragraph is the one part of this log nothing verifies,
so this one states only what was checked. The census over all 196 unclaimed
lines closes the question it was run to answer: there is no rule in this book
that reaches nothing and that a census over those lines could see. The two
real gaps the parameter sweep left are **features, not oversights, and both
are already recorded in CLAUDE.md §6** — `Character.weapons` (weapons are not
editable, which is what `ParryBlock` has been waiting on since M0) and
`Character.secondaryDelta` (`SavedEdits` covers the four attributes and bought
skills, and pp. 8-9 price six secondary characteristics nothing can buy).
Either is a schema change to `SavedEdits` plus real UI, and **`SessionStore
.load` discards the WHOLE file on a decode failure**, so either has to widen
additively or drop every existing save — the same constraint 6cb recorded for
the instanced traits.

So the next slice needs a fresh sweep, and every direction already run expires
rather than standing: fields for a reader (6ai), functions for a caller (6cf),
rows for a consumer (6ci), files for a loader (6dg), strings a screen types
(6cq), seams between claimed spans (6ba), rules the app contradicts, what the
tests know that production does not (6bz), and now parameters with no
non-default argument (6dz). One grep per named artefact is what checking this
paragraph costs.

**One loose end, stated so it is not inherited as settled:** the divination
backlash disappearing when a push clears a critical failure is correct by
construction — `Result` is handed `backlash?.takeIf { answer.isCritical }` —
and has not been seen on a device, because a margin-based critical failure on
a target a push can carry is a state a 3d6 roll reaches rarely. It is a
reading of two lines, not a test and not a device check.
